title: W16-A: pure workflow_control decision module (grant+confirmed-ownership preconditions, observer-only and guessed-action refusal, requested/acknowledged/result receipt); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Every `workflow_*` Pi tool and every `workbench:*` grant check lives in src/index.ts (hot, Sr. Engineer-owned), and native Furnace control would live in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts (hot). W16's acceptance "compact bounded result and ACL" still needs a testable control core. Deliver it as ONE new source file and ONE new test file; register nothing.

src/workbench/control.ts (new), pure and provider-free:
- `interface NativeControlRequest { scope: ObservationScope; principal: { id: string; role?: string }; grants: readonly string[] | undefined; target: NativeRef; action: string; params?: JsonValue; invocationId: string; requestedAt: string }` (names follow docs/workbench/13 Host boundary `requestControl(req: NativeControlRequest): Promise<NativeControlReceipt>`; this bead implements the decision, not the host method).
- `decideControl(request, deps: { projection: ObservationProjection; now: () => string })` returns `{ decision: 'denied'; category: CapabilityErrorCategory; reason: string }` or `{ decision: 'permitted'; receipt: NativeControlReceipt }`.
- `NativeControlReceipt` phases are distinct and ordered: `requested` -> `acknowledged` -> `result`. Fields: contractVersion 'workbench.control/v1', requestId, principal, grant, policy (rule name), target, action, invocationId, ownershipConfirmationRef, requestedAt; `acknowledge(receipt, { acknowledgedAt, nativeAckRef })` and `settle(receipt, { outcome: 'completed'|'failed'|'cancelled'|'unknown'; nativeResultRef: string; settledAt })` return new frozen receipts and throw CapabilityError('validation') on out-of-order transitions or missing native references. The module never calls a provider, never mutates the projection, never fabricates acknowledged/result.
- Deny rules (first match wins, every rule has a test): grants undefined/non-array/non-string entries or any wildcard (`control:*`) -> authorization "unknown permission data"; grants containing only discover:/inspect:/observe: prefixes -> authorization "observer-only" regardless of action spelling (stop, STOP, terminate, __proto__); action not in the frozen per-provider allowlist (furnace: stop; claude-agent-sdk: interrupt; forge: cancel) -> validation "unknown action"; missing exact grant `control:<provider>.<action>` -> authorization; target key not in the request scope (different workspace/principal) -> authorization "cross-scope"; target lacking a projection `ownership` relation whose provenance.source === target.provider AND provenance.nativeConfirmationRef is a non-empty string (re-check both; do not trust the relation kind alone) -> authorization "no confirmed lifecycle ownership" (causation/grouping/hypothesis edges never qualify); destructive actions (stop, cancel, interrupt, kill, delete) without `params.confirmed === true` -> validation "operator confirmation required".
test/workbench-control.test.ts (new): one test per rule plus the phase-ordering falsifiers; no TTY, no providers, no network.
Out of scope: any edit to src/index.ts, src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts or other hot files; Pi tool registration; executing a native stop. If the worker finds registration necessary to satisfy acceptance, stop and return blocked.

title: VC-4/W13: Furnace observer projects Attempt nodes, Run->Attempt ownership edges and source intervals (additive)
description:
Gap: nothing in src/ calls ObservationProjection.relate(), so the W15 inspector's graph/overview/timeline never receive a real native edge; FurnaceObserver.projectionSnapshot() (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts) emits a single Run node and flattens Attempt IDs into evidenceRefs with no Run->Attempt edge and no attempt interval, although FurnaceReading already carries attempts.items[{id,runId,workId,state,outcome,startedAt,finishedAt}] and the native attempts request ID.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): add FurnaceObserver.projectionTopology(reading) returning the unchanged Run snapshot plus one NativeSnapshot per returned Attempt (type 'attempt', bounded intervals from native started_at/finished_at only) and one 'ownership' relation Run->Attempt whose provenance.source is 'furnace' and whose nativeConfirmationRef is the attempts page requestId (the producer's own page asserts attempt.run_id === run.run_id). Partial pages produce no edges for the missing tail; stale readings throw like projectionSnapshot. projectionSnapshot() stays byte-for-byte compatible because src/index.ts:2560 (hot) consumes it; wiring projectionTopology into the Pi observe tool is a separate Sr. Engineer follow-up and is NOT part of this bead.

Files: src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts; test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts (or new test/workbench-furnace-topology.test.ts). Reuse the existing client() mock fixture style. Specs: docs/workbench/09 (Relationships are typed and provenanced; Acceptance/negative controls), docs/workbench/15 VC-4, docs/workbench/02 WB-025/WB-037, docs/workbench/10 Four views (Timeline).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first tests in test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts (extend; never delete existing cases) or a new test/workbench-furnace-topology.test.ts, then minimal implementation in src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts ONLY. Hot files (src/index.ts, src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts, ...) must not be touched; keep projectionSnapshot() signature and behavior unchanged because src/index.ts:2560 consumes it.

A1. New additive method FurnaceObserver.projectionTopology(reading: FurnaceReading): { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: FurnaceObservedRelation[] } where FurnaceObservedRelation is exactly the parameter type of ObservationProjection.relate. snapshots[0] deep-equals projectionSnapshot(reading); then one NativeSnapshot per reading.attempts.items entry with source {provider:'furnace', type:'attempt', id:item.id, scope:reading.source.workspaceRoot}, kind 'furnace.attempt.snapshot', node.type 'sdk-operation', statusText item.state (and outcome when present), trace {invocationId: <same as run>, correlationIds:{runId,workId}}, interval ONLY when item.startedAt exists and endedAt ONLY when item.finishedAt exists. No Work node is invented (no Work DTO is read); workId is a correlation id only.
   Quote: docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-025 "Workbench distinguishes Run/Work/Attempt, Forge operation and workspace basis, Claude session, HX coverage, RF provenance."

A2. Exactly one relation per returned attempt: {from: run ref, to: attempt ref, kind:'ownership', provenance:{source:'furnace', observedAt: reading.observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: reading.source.requestIds.attempts}}. No 'dependency', 'causation' or 'hypothesis' edge is ever emitted by this method (test asserts every relation.kind === 'ownership').
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)" and "Store edge provenance with timestamp and source". Quote: docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Vertical cuts" VC-4: "Derived tree/timeline shows observed rather than invented edges."

A3. Partial pages: when reading.attempts.complete === false or attempts.unreadableCount > 0, relations exist only for returned items and the Run snapshot coverage stays 'partial'; nothing is synthesized for the missing tail.
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Acceptance/negative controls" item 5: "Simulated missing relation; no fabricated dependency edge or precise critical path."

A4. Stale/disconnected reading (freshness !== 'current' or connection !== 'connected') throws CapabilityError category 'unavailable' exactly as projectionSnapshot does; no partial topology is returned.
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Experimental projection implementation": "stale readings cannot refresh confirmed projection state."

A5. Integration proof against the real read model: apply snapshots via projection.refresh and relations via projection.relate on a real ObservationProjection; then projection.query({scope, parent: runRef, limit: 10}) returns exactly the attempt nodes; layoutInspector(...,{view:'graph'}) output contains 'ownership' and '[furnace]'; the timeline view prints a source interval for an attempt with startedAt+finishedAt and 'timing unavailable' for an attempt lacking started_at.
   Quote: docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four views" Timeline: "Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps."

A6. Observer close still invokes zero control verbs (existing assertion pattern: stop/pause/resume/retry mocks have no calls) and no raw log line or redacted secret appears in any snapshot or relation (JSON.stringify(...) does not contain 'TOPSECRET').
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Acceptance/negative controls" item 8: "Closing observer causes zero cancellation calls."

A7. Gate: ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files clean; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts test/workbench-inspector.test.ts green; record red and green commands in the delivered ledger line. Do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).

title: W12 fault gap: a non-read node() leaves no journal row until it settles (runtime.ts appends only after await callNode), so a kill after the provider side effect but before the host result, or after the result but before the append, leaves nothing for the resume tripwire and the next resume re-runs the effect live (duplicate effect); record a dispatched row before the call so a resume refuses that position as uncertain-effect until an operator reconciles it
description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g2 round 5, run g2-work-r1; measured at rig origin/workbench/implementation-program e830ac2 = BOUNDARY base at groom time; anchors from git show e830ac2:<path>):

src/workflow/runtime.ts records a node() journal row only when the call settles: the live path appends at :1509 (ok true) or :1533 (ok false), both AFTER `const output = await callNode({...})` (:1482); the only pre-settlement append is the carry-forward of an already-refused entry (:1417). The admission at :1305-:1313 treats `nodeJournal.get(index) === undefined` as `{ kind: "live" }`. journal.ts:213 documents "Append one settled call. Failure to write is not failure to run." and its header promises that for any non-read effect class "the resume stops on it rather than re-running or silently replaying an effect the previous run already performed." That tripwire exists only once a row exists. Consequence: a process kill (or host crash) between the provider side effect and the host result, or between the result and the append, leaves NO row at that position, so the next resume admits the position as live and performs the effect AGAIN — the duplicate effect docs/08 forbids. docs/14 names both locations as required fault-injection points and no test exercises them (grep over test/ for "before journal append|before host result|dispatched row" returns nothing; test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts covers only recorded rows; wb-tu1 covers a recorded row with an absent class).

Scope (atomic; W12 side-effect policy; owner ruling requested on the row shape before claim, see notes):
1. Red first, test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts: a fixture capability with a non-read effect class and an exactly-once effect counter; the host seam throws/kills after the effect counter increments but before the result reaches the runtime (location "after provider side effect but before host result"), and a second variant settles the result but fails the append (location "after result before journal append", journal append seam injected to throw once). Today the resume re-runs the node: the counter reaches 2. Quote the counter in the red note.
2. Fix shape (proposed, owner may reshape): immediately before `await callNode` (after nodeSemaphore.acquire and the aborted/settled check) and ONLY when the current effect class is not "read" (including an absent class, mirroring wb-tu1's fail-closed reading), append a dispatched row `{ kind: "node", index, key: key ?? "", ok: false, capabilityId, effectClass (when defined), basis, dispatched: true }` through the same recordJournal seam. The settled row at the same index supersedes it on read (nodeJournal is a Map built last-wins per index, runtime.ts:719-721), so a completed run resumes exactly as today. On resume a dispatched row with no settled successor is refused at :1313 as uncertain-effect (the existing non-read refusal), the workflow_node event carries reconcile.state "pending", the hint names the producer and position, and the row is carried forward verbatim; workflow_reconcile inspect reports the position with outcome "unrecorded" (dispatched, never settled). Read-class nodes write no pre-call row: journals of read-only and agent-only workflows stay byte-identical (existing journal fixtures and assertions untouched).
3. isEntry (journal.ts:229) accepts the optional `dispatched: true` marker (anything else drops the line as mangled, as today); journal-compat.ts MIRRORS the runtime (never re-implements): a dispatched row classifies node-effectful with the dispatched marker in its census and no new class unless the owner rules one; test/workflow-journal-compat.test.ts gains the mirror case. Reconcile acknowledge/override over a dispatched row bind by entryDigest exactly as over a failed row.
4. docs/workbench/08 "Side-effect replay policy on resume" gains one sentence naming the dispatched row (owner-authored or in the same commit per the owner's ruling) and TRACEABILITY gains the row; node qa/workbench/status-ledger.mjs --strict exits 0 before delivery (12:10Z seat rule).

Open questions for the owner (recorded in notes): Q1 marker shape (`dispatched: true` vs a failure-shaped row with no marker); Q2 whether a FAILED pre-call append on a non-read node refuses the call fail-closed or keeps journal.ts's "failure to write is not failure to run" (today's policy); Q3 whether the Claude host's settled-agent prefix needs the same pre-call row for agents with non-read gates (out of scope unless ruled in).

Non-scope: no change to read replay (same effect class, basis and key, marked stale), no change to the reconcile grants (never mint reconcile:*), no change to agent prefix semantics, no change to the admission order ("Decided synchronously, before anything yields"). Files: src/workflow/runtime.ts, src/workflow/journal.ts, src/workflow/journal-compat.ts, test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts, test/workflow-journal-compat.test.ts, docs/workbench/08 + TRACEABILITY (ruling-dependent). Serialized after wb-tu1 (same two source files; blocked-by). Tier: sonnet (multi-module, safety invariant).

Required outcomes: reconciliation/uncertainty/conflict; no duplicate effects, no invented PASS, no implicit mass cancellation." -> the resume refuses the position with CapabilityError category "uncertain-effect", the workflow_node event carries reconcile.state "pending" with the producer and position, and the operator reconcile journey (inspect -> evidence -> acknowledge/override) is the only way forward, exactly as for a settled non-read row. B6. docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md section "Compatibility feature control": "Ensure older journal format remains readable when supported" -> journals without the marker read exactly as today; journal-compat.ts mirrors the runtime with a mirror test. description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g2 round 5, run g2-work-r1; OWNER-DIRECTED filing per BOUNDARY 2026-10-15T13:30Z "wb-9x5.3 respin rulings": "F2 (real evidence channel, loadedPayload retired) + F3 wall-time p50/p95 = GROOM FILES a W21 follow-up bead (trunk >= ccb0fc8 harness), not blocked, not this respin." Measured at rig origin/workbench/implementation-program e830ac2 = BOUNDARY base at groom time; ccb0fc8 (wb-6ze.17, host-built EvidenceStore wired into the inspector dialog) is an ancestor of the tip.)

The wb-9x5.3 retained-memory receipt (in respin, gate cmd_b2e62ac8008d) proves post-GC retention bounds with payload bytes carried by a stand-in field (loadedPayload) that the inspector never reads (gate finding F2), and records neither bench wall time nor peak allocation (F3). Since ccb0fc8 the REAL evidence channel is on trunk: src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts EvidenceStore (request/get/abort/abortAll with {loaders; maxEntries; maxBytes; timeoutMs}), wired by the inspector dialog so Enter on a selected ref calls store.request, the details view renders from the synchronous store.get, and close calls abortAll. Nothing measures retained memory or wall time when large payload previews actually flow through that store under grouped-10k navigation.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, src untouched, hot files untouched):
- qa/workbench/inspector-evidence-retained-bench.mjs (new; dist imports only; reuses qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs): builds the grouped-10k fixture whose operation nodes list evidence refs, supplies a FIXTURE EvidenceLoader (fixture-named, never a real producer) whose load() returns bounded EvidenceContent previews derived from large payload buffers, constructs the EvidenceStore with header-stated bench-only budgets, and drives N navigation cycles through the SAME dialog/reducer path an operator uses: select node -> Enter (store.request) -> details render from store.get -> blur/selection change -> close (abortAll). Per cycle it records wall time (performance.now) and, after an explicit GC under --expose-gc at a header-stated warmup anchor, process.memoryUsage heapUsed/external; it reports p50/p95/max wall time, peak heapUsed between GCs, bytes offered vs bytes retained post-GC, loaded/aborted/unavailable entry counts, focusedCycles and detailsCycles judged equal to cycles (exit 2 otherwise, as ruled for wb-9x5.3 F1).
- Falsifiers in the same receipt: (a) release: after close/abortAll and GC, retained bytes attributable to evidence previews return to the stated floor and no loaded entry survives the store budget; (b) positive control: a deliberately retained payload reference is DETECTED as retained and released when dropped; (c) budget: the store never holds more than maxEntries entries or maxBytes preview bytes, and raw payload buffers are never reachable from a loaded entry (preview-only).
- Bounds (stated in the file header before any measurement, per the wb-9x5.4 bench rule bound at 13:05Z): retained-heap bound, wall-time bound, warmup anchor, bench-only limits (fixture size, maxEntries, maxBytes, timeoutMs) as constants with the disclosure "non-comparable to production (bench limits ... vs production ...)" copied into the receipt. A miss exits 1 and is recorded as a miss; off-shape exits 2; never a silent drop.
- Receipt: workbench.evidence-retained-bench/v1 to stdout and $W21_RECEIPT when set: utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD + dirty flag), node, toolchain versions, host {platform, arch, cpus, model}, fixture, limits, bounds, cycles, series, outliers, verdict.

title: VC-6/W14: pure latency-decomposition selector over ObservationProjection source intervals (per-class union/busy ms for model/build/context/queue/query/host/other by frozen provider map; open or missing intervals counted, never summed; wall from the closed root interval else unknown; overhead only when every interval is closed and page complete; tokens unknown unless native usage given; MeasuredMetric rows for compareWorkflowRuns); designer.ts, attention.ts, wiring excluded
description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g1 round 4, run g2-work-r1; measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program cd5aab7; src/workbench and src/index.ts are byte-identical at the b4ca4aa tip at filing; anchors from git show cd5aab7:<path>):

docs/workbench/09 section "Aggregates and profiling" requires latency decomposition derived "only with valid source intervals" and docs/workbench/11 section "Comparative experiment protocol" requires separating "model tokens, provider waiting, Forge build time, RF context time, external queue and overlay overhead when telemetry allows". Nothing in src/workbench computes any of it: git grep -i 'decompos\|latency' over src/workbench at cd5aab7 matches only a comment (capability-registry.ts:323). The projection already carries the inputs: ObservedNode.interval {startedAt, endedAt?} (observation.ts:10, :74), nativeRef.provider (:58), presentation.statusTone (:8), freshness and sourceConnectionState (:63-65), invocationId (:70); query() pages are bounded by maxQuery (default 100, :93) and report truncated. attention.ts (wb-6ze.4) measures OPEN intervals against a caller clock and a dependency-chain critical path; timeline.ts renders lanes; neither sums or attributes closed time by provider. designer.ts compareWorkflowRuns (:217) consumes CompareRun.metrics: readonly MeasuredMetric[] (:179, :185), but the registered workflow_compare tool fills metrics: [] (src/index.ts:2554), so every comparison today reports verdict unknown for want of a measured source (docs/11 section "Experimental read-only source tools": "Missing native measured metrics yields unknown, not a claimed optimization.").

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new module src/workbench/latency.ts and ONE new test test/workbench-latency.test.ts.
- Export LATENCY_CONTRACT = "workbench.latency-decomposition/v1" (a new single-carrier literal; wb-cax.8's rule), a frozen LATENCY_CLASSES ["model", "build", "context", "queue", "query", "host", "other"] and a frozen provider map {claude-agent-sdk: model, forge: build, reactivefiber: context, furnace: queue, hyperunix: query, pi-workflow: host}; any other provider is "other" (never a guess from a title or kind).
- selectLatencyDecomposition(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query">, input: {scope; invocationId; limit?: 1..100 default 100; usage?: readonly {source: NativeRef; inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; evidenceRefs: readonly string[]}[]}) -> LatencyDecomposition {contract; basis: "observed"; invocationId; examined {nodes, truncated}; wall: {measured: true; ms; from: "root-interval"} | {measured: false; reasons}; components: one entry per class {class; providers (sorted, sanitized, bounded to 64 chars); nodes; intervals {closed, open, missing}; busyMs (sum of closed intervals); unionMs (union of closed intervals so concurrency never double-counts); measured: boolean; reasons}; waiting: {nodes; reasons: ["single-interval-per-node"]} (the projection holds one interval per node, so a waiting/executing split is unknown with that reason, never estimated); tokens: {measured: true; input; output; sources} only from supplied usage whose source matches an examined node's nativeRef, else {measured: false; reasons: ["no-native-usage"]}; overhead: {measured: true; ms} = wall minus the union of every component's closed intervals ONLY when wall is measured, examined.truncated is false and every examined interval is closed, else {measured: false; reasons}; caveat: one frozen constant stating closed source intervals only and unreconciled cross-provider clocks}. Reasons come from a frozen vocabulary (page-truncated, open-intervals, missing-intervals, no-root-interval, no-native-usage, single-interval-per-node).
- Export toMeasuredMetrics(report, {subjectBasis; freshness}) -> MeasuredMetric[] (designer.ts:179 shape; names latency.<class>.unionMs, latency.<class>.busyMs, latency.wall.ms, latency.overhead.ms; unit "ms"; source = the invocation's root nativeRef; coverage "complete" only when examined.truncated is false and the component's intervals.open + missing === 0, "partial" when some intervals are open or missing, "unknown" when nothing was measured; evidenceRefs from the examined nodes, bounded) so a caller can feed compareWorkflowRuns without any edit to designer.ts.
- Mirror attention.ts: refuse a bad limit with CapabilityError("validation", ...); re-check scope and invocationId on every page row (attention.ts:281); the wall comes from the examined node of presentation.type "workflow" for the invocation (the root) and only when its interval is closed; no clock, no Date.now, no Math.random; an interval whose instant is not a bounded timezone-qualified ISO-8601 string counts as missing; provider strings pass the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (stripUnsafeText today; the single exported display helper once wb-952's respin lands) and a 64-char bound before they appear in output; no raw payloads, titles or evidence bodies in the report.

Non-scope: designer.ts, attention.ts, timeline.ts, observation.ts, src/index.ts and any Pi tool or dialog wiring (the workflow_compare reply builder is wb-69g.7; the metrics hookup into the registered tool is a later index.ts wiring bead under the BOUNDARY 12:25Z serialization rule); no estimate of a waiting/executing split; no critical path (attention.ts owns it); no token derivation from anything but supplied native usage.
acceptance_criteria:
All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig at origin/workbench/implementation-program cd5aab7 (identical at b4ca4aa). Red-first: test/workbench-latency.test.ts fails before src/workbench/latency.ts exists.
L1. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics." and "Derive latency decomposition only with valid source intervals." -> only closed intervals (both bounds valid ISO instants) contribute to busyMs and unionMs; an open interval and a missing or malformed one are counted under intervals.open / intervals.missing and never summed; a static assertion proves the module source contains neither Date.now nor Math.random nor a now parameter.
L2. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "Comparative experiment protocol": "Separate model tokens, provider waiting, Forge build time, RF context time, external queue and overlay overhead when telemetry allows." -> a fixture with claude-agent-sdk, forge, reactivefiber, furnace and hyperunix nodes yields one component per class with providers listed, and unionMs < busyMs when two same-class intervals overlap; an unknown provider lands in "other"; waiting is reported with reason single-interval-per-node; tokens are measured only from supplied usage whose source matches an examined nativeRef (a usage row with a foreign source is ignored and the reason no-native-usage stands).
L3. docs/workbench/11 section "Comparative experiment protocol": "Decline precise claim if trace coverage insufficient; include raw evidence references." and section "Experimental read-only source tools": "Missing native measured metrics yields unknown, not a claimed optimization." -> overhead is measured only when wall is measured, examined.truncated is false and every examined interval is closed; a page larger than limit marks examined.truncated true, every component carries reason page-truncated and toMeasuredMetrics coverage is "partial" or "unknown", never "complete"; wall is unknown with reason no-root-interval when the root node has no closed interval.
L4. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-038: "Versioned plan/execute/observe comparison uses immutable source and config digest references." and docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Vertical cuts" VC-6: "executes comparison with real native evidence; reports gains/confounders." -> toMeasuredMetrics rows satisfy designer.ts MeasuredMetric and, fed as CompareRun.metrics for a reference and a candidate run sharing one basis, compareWorkflowRuns reports the latency metrics as measured with reference and candidate summaries; with mismatched bases the existing confound behaviour is unchanged (designer.ts untouched, proven by git diff).
L5. Scope and bounds: a page row from another scope or invocation is dropped (attention.ts:281 precedent); a limit outside 1..100 is a typed CapabilityError validation refusal; the report for 100 nodes serialises under 8 KiB; provider strings carrying terminal escapes, bidi controls or zero-width characters are stripped and bounded through src/workbench/redaction.ts.
L6. Mutation table in the delivery note: summing open intervals, summing busy where union is reported, defaulting an unknown provider to model, measuring overhead on a truncated page, and minting tokens from node count each fail a named test.
Process: ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files; no any; no inline imports; never weaken or delete existing tests; git diff <base>..HEAD -- src/ touches only src/workbench/latency.ts; grep -n 'workflow-script/v1' over the diff returns nothing; forge run lint / typing / test green in the worktree; base b4ca4aa or later (origin tip at claim time; read BOUNDARY.md at task start, before claiming and before pushing).

title: W06/W19 defect (from the wb-6hb.4 parity falsifier): the claude-tool surface capability_invoke PERMITS a prototype-key input because zod strips a declared __proto__ key before the provider sees it, while the oracle and both node() surfaces refuse 'Prototype pollution key at invoke(...) input.__proto__.'; refuse prototype keys on the raw input BEFORE schema parsing so every surface shares one input contract (docs/06)
description: Gap (owner ruling on the wb-6hb.4 gate finding, measured at cd5aab7 with zod 4.6.7): for an input object carrying an own __proto__ (or constructor / prototype) key at any depth, the oracle in capability-registry refuses with the fixed text 'Prototype pollution key at invoke(...) input.__proto__.' and both node() surfaces refuse at the VM boundary, but the curated claude-tool surface (src/workbench/claude-capability-tools.ts) parses the raw input with a zod record schema first, which silently STRIPS the key, so the call is PERMITTED and the provider receives the stripped object. Graded Low-Medium: no authority escalation (the key never reaches the provider or the InvocationContext), but a breach of docs/06 'identical authorization and input contracts' across surfaces — a surface permitting what the oracle refuses is a widening by the falsifier's definition. Scope: scan the RAW tool input for prototype keys (own keys __proto__, constructor, prototype, at any depth, arrays included) before any zod parse, and refuse with exactly the oracle's text through the same sanitized reply path; share the scan with the registry oracle (one exported predicate, not a copy); add the cell to the wb-6hb.4 parity table and FLIP its pinned known-widening assertion in the same commit. (:155), buildWorkflowInspectReply(snapshot, grants, target, view?, bounds?) (:250), capabilityCatalogEntries(providers) (:94), INSPECT_VIEWS (:41), TOOL_REPLY_CONTRACT_VERSION "workbench.tool-reply/v1" and the TOOL_REPLY_* bounds (:14-18). Nothing consumes them: src/index.ts imports no ./workbench/tool-replies.js (:69-77 list every workbench import), the registered workbench_catalog tool (:2493-2502) hand-maps registryFor(ctx.cwd).discover({grants}) to seven descriptor fields with no filter, limit, cursor, contract version or explicit byte-cap marker, and no inspect tool is registered at all (grep workflow_inspect|workbench_inspect|buildWorkflowInspectReply over src/: none) although docs/11 lists workflow_inspect as a first public Pi tool and docs/06 defines its exact inspect:<capabilityId> ACL. The W16 acceptance "compact bounded result and ACL" (docs/15) therefore holds for the pure module but not for the Pi surface an operator or model can reach.

Scope (atomic, wiring only): edit registerWorkbenchTools in src/index.ts and add ONE new test file test/workbench-pi-tool-replies.test.ts (boot the real extension in claude mode through test/helpers/boot-extension.ts).
- workbench_catalog: parameters gain filter (string), limit (integer, bounds from TOOL_REPLY_MAX_LIMIT never a spelled literal) and cursor (string); execute builds the snapshot with capabilityCatalogEntries over the providers registered for ctx.cwd and returns sanitizeWorkbenchJsonText(buildWorkflowCatalogReply(snapshot, grants(ctx), {filter, limit, cursor})) so the reply carries the contract version, stable cursor pagination, the byte-cap marker and ONLY capabilities whose exact discover:<id> grant is held (absent, never an error row). Provider access: index.ts already holds the provider instances it registers (registryFor / native-modules registration order); keep a per-workspace provider list beside the registry. ONLY if red proves that impossible without duplicating state, add one additive read-only accessor to CapabilityRegistry (e.g. providers(): readonly CapabilityProvider[]) with no change to register/discover/invoke/inspect semantics.
- workflow_inspect (docs/11 name; the owner may rule workbench_inspect for namespace consistency - adopt the ruling, never both): parameters {target: string (1..200), view?: one of INSPECT_VIEWS (the Type union derived from the exported constant)}; execute returns sanitizeWorkbenchJsonText(buildWorkflowInspectReply(snapshot, grants(ctx), target, view)). The builder's typed errors (invalid-target, unknown-view, unknown-target, unavailable with not-granted / inspect-not-advertised / inspect-not-implemented) are the reply; no raw error text, no stack, no fallback to registry.inspect() (the tool is metadata only - a provider's invoke and inspect are never called by either tool).
- Registration hygiene: both tools register from the same session_start gate (workflowAgentBackend "claude"), once per process (workbenchToolsRegistered guard), with the same grants(ctx) source as the other workbench tools; the legacy Agent/SubagentWorkflow surface and tool names are untouched (WB-011). Per-verb citation (the test pins every quoted line verbatim against node_modules):
- cancel (the only verb; NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS.forge, control.ts:19): dist/operation.d.ts:77 "cancel(operationId: string): Promise<CancelReceipt>;" on OperationClient; dist/operation.js:38 CANCEL_METHOD "operation.cancel"; :108 request(CANCEL_METHOD, { operation_id: operationId }) decoded by decodeCancelResponse (dist/cancellation.js:49-67).
- answer semantics: dist/cancellation.d.ts:43 cancellationEstablished: false (an ack never establishes); :38-39 + cancellation.js:66 the receipt's operationId is the CALLER's value (measured: decodeCancelResponse("op-x", {operation_id:"op-y",...}) returns operationId "op-x"), and the decoder admits any roster pair (NOT_REQUESTED+ACCEPTED decodes). So attribution requires Forge's own raw.operation_id echo, and the adapter, not the decoder, rejects contradictory axes.
- establishment: dist/event_delivery_policy.d.ts:47-49 terminal_disposition / CANCELLATION_DISPOSITION "cancelled-established", reaching a caller as OperationEnd (dist/operation_stream.d.ts:100-106).
- no-cancel modes: dist/fallback.d.ts:106 "cancel(): never;"; fallback.js:76 CLI_ONESHOT_CAPABILITIES cancel: unsupported (its cancel throws UnsupportedCapability, "sent nothing", errors.d.ts:84-95). App servers enumerate {method, available} per wire name (Forge src/forge/app_server/lifecycle.py:167), so the app-server key is "operation.cancel" (same rule as providers/forge.ts:90 for gate.status).
- server context (Forge HEAD f62193b551, NOT the pinned server, UNDETERMINED for the pinned version): operation_cancellation.py binds operation.cancel; operation_manager.py:1840-1907 ACCEPTED = {operation_id, cancel_intent CANCEL_REQUESTED, cancel_acceptance ACCEPTED, cancellation_established false}; refusals add establishment NOT_ATTEMPTED (:1812-1838); unknown id -> operation_not_found, malformed params -> invalid_params (protocol.py:62-63), both before any lookup or actuation; the cancelled terminal is the original request's RESULT frame with result.terminal_disposition and result.operation_id (_cancellation_answer :743-771).

OUTCOME MAPPING
- refused (ForgeControlRefusal, nothing sent, zero seam calls): denied-decision (core category + policy), unvetted-decision, permit-consumed, unsupported-verb (provider != forge or type != operation), invalid-target (id outside ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$), invalid-deps, foreign-workspace (request scope != workspaceRoot, or a STATED target scope != workspaceRoot), capability-unavailable (category unavailable; frozen surface {declaration, seamMethod present|absent|refused, mode, state = stateOf("operation.cancel"), facadeState = stateOf("cancel")}), aborted-before-issue. Sends only when the seam carries cancel AND state === supported AND facadeState !== unsupported.
- acknowledged: ACCEPTED + CANCEL_REQUESTED, receipt and payload consistent, raw.operation_id === target.id, cancellationEstablished false on both -> core acknowledge, nativeAckRef forge-operation:<id>:operation.cancel:CANCEL_REQUESTED:ACCEPTED. Never settled by execute.
- not-accepted (receipt stays requested): REFUSED_NOT_FOUND | REFUSED_NOT_CANCELLABLE | REFUSED_ALREADY_TERMINAL with NOT_REQUESTED (axes + establishment echoed), or ServerError serverCode operation_not_found | invalid_params (serverCode only echoed).
- uncertain (parked, never retried): seam-failure (failure {code: SDK code label or unknown, serverCode when FORGE_SERVER_ERROR}), wait-timeout, wait-aborted, unattributable-answer, contradictory-answer, receipt-refused.
- settleForgeControl(execution, OperationEnd, now): only an acknowledged execution this module returned; forge_terminal whose result.operation_id === target.id and kebab-case disposition -> core settle: cancelled-established -> cancelled, any other -> unknown, nativeResultRef forge-operation:<id>:terminal_disposition=<d>; transport_terminal -> uncertain transport-terminal; else no-terminal-echo; an uncertain attempt leaves it settleable; at most one result.

DEVIATIONS AND CAVEATS (owner rulings requested on D1, D2, C1)
D1 A non-cancellation terminal settles outcome "unknown" with Forge's disposition quoted, never "completed"/"failed": the vendored SDK declares only CANCELLATION_DISPOSITION; every other disposition is unmodeled vocabulary, so a verdict read off it would be invented (docs/08:56 "no invented PASS").
D2 The result phase is a second export, settleForgeControl(execution, OperationEnd), not a wait inside execute: a CancelReceipt can never establish, and waiting for the operation's own terminal would hold the control call for the operation's lifetime. Mirrors the wb-69g.8 ruling (3) (result only from what the observer later reports). The host (wb-cra) feeds handle.result() resolution/rejection as forge_terminal/transport_terminal.
D3 The pre-effect server codes come from the Forge HEAD server source; the vendored SDK declares no server codes (ServerError.serverCode passes through verbatim). A renamed code degrades to uncertain, never a false not-accepted; any other ServerError (e.g. internal_error, which can follow the token being set inside request_cancel) is uncertain.
D4 The capability gate is fail-closed beyond the SDK's tri-state: "unknown" refuses too (as providers/forge.ts:90-92 does for gate.status), and a map stating the facade name "cancel" unsupported refuses even beside operation.cancel supported.
C1 Forge operation ids are per app-server session: the wiring must hand over the OperationClient over the connection that started the operation (otherwise Forge answers operation_not_found -> not-accepted, harmless). The adapter cannot observe which connection started it; OperationClient.handleOf(id) would be a stricter local precondition if preferred (not used: it is null unless the registry was attached before the started frame).
C2 workspaceRoot mirrors wb-69g.3's foreign-workspace guard. An unscoped target is accepted because src/index.ts:2777 projects native SDK nodes { provider, type: "operation", id } with no scope; a stated foreign scope, or a request scoped elsewhere, is refused.

## 2026-10-15 14:53Z (system UTC) flywheel orchestrator — OWNER RULING F8 (wb-0kg.5 gate): ownership vs actionability for local-detached control
Host loss does NOT withdraw ownership confirmation — ownership is identity, not liveness (the invocation -> host-process edge survives host loss by design). Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/claude-control.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-claude-control.test.ts. The adapter consumes a decideControl result for target.provider "claude-agent-sdk" plus an injected session seam -- an interface the adapter DEFINES and the host will later satisfy, e.g. `{ interrupt(session: NativeRef): Promise<SDKControlInterruptResponse | undefined> }`, fake in tests exactly like the injected invoke seam in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts and the wb-69g.3 pattern. 2. Denied decisions (every ControlDenyPolicy, including "operator-confirmation" for the destructive interrupt and "missing-exact-grant" for a revoked control:claude-agent-sdk.interrupt grant) return a typed sanitized refusal; the seam call count is 0.
3. Permitted decision -> the seam is called exactly once with the receipt's target; the adapter never retries (park-not-retry): a seam rejection or timeout settles outcome "failed" (or stays "requested" when the rejection precedes any acknowledgment) with a redacted diagnostic category, never a second interrupt.
4. Acknowledgment echoes, never minted: a resolved SDKControlInterruptResponse becomes the acknowledged phase with nativeAckRef derived from the real receipt and the still_queued uuid COUNT (uuids themselves sanitized, never raw); an `undefined` resolution ("Older CLIs") acknowledges with a named no-receipt marker, never a fabricated uuid.
5. Transport success is never domain verification: a resolved interrupt never yields outcome "completed" or "cancelled" by itself; the result phase is settled only from an observed terminal supplied by the caller (projection), otherwise outcome "unknown" with the docs/06 uncertain wording.
6. Every string that can reach an operator (diagnostics, ack refs, refusal text) routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (strip, redact, strip); byte-bounded.
7. Audit: every receipt phase carries the ControlReceiptCore audit fields unchanged from the core (control.ts:40-54); the adapter adds nothing to and removes nothing from them.

Out of scope: Pi workflow_control registration (src/index.ts), host retention of the Query handle (claude-host.ts), live SDK or claude-live tier, control.ts edits, Furnace/local-detached/forge legs (wb-69g.3, wb-0kg.6).

title: defect(wb-g1g.2): topology slice silently undercounts remainder and labels trace observed when projection maxQuery (prod 40) is below requested relationPage (default 100)
description:
Found by flywheel adversarial review run g1-r3 of branch machine/flywheel/wb-g1g.2 (commit 54e4dcc, gate receipt cmd_87383785df8f, which carried this as finding topology-slice-silent-page-cap-undercount, CONFIRMED medium, ownerRulingNeeded).

Defect: selectLinkedTopology silently undercounts the remainder and mislabels the trace "observed" whenever the projection's own relation-page cap (ObservationLimits.maxQuery) is below the selector's requested relationPage (default 100).

Mechanism (verified in code at 54e4dcc): src/workbench/observation.ts:624-625 relations() clamps limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery) and reports no truncation; src/workbench/topology-slice.ts readSide() computes full = rows.length >= page against the REQUESTED page, so a page clamped below the request is indistinguishable from a complete read. The only guard is a doc comment on TopologyCaps.relationPage ("Must not exceed the projection's own page cap") — nothing enforces it, and the DEFAULT (100) violates it for the production projection, which is constructed with maxQuery 40 (wb-6ze.27 description, measured at 24e6015: src/index.ts:2380; W21 bench qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36 also pins 40).

Independent runtime reproduction (review worktree at 54e4dcc, real ObservationProjection, vitest): new ObservationProjection({maxQuery: 40}); 45 observed dependency edges F->n00..n44; selectLinkedTopology default caps returned downstream 10 listed, remainder {count: 30, atLeast: false}, trace {label: "observed", reasons: []}. Truth: 45 observed matching edges, so the true remainder is 35 — 5 observed edges silently dropped, the count claimed exact, and completeness claimed. Control: caps {relationPage: 40} correctly returns remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace with reasons ["relations-truncated"]. This corroborates the gate seat's probe (10 listed + remainder 30 atLeast false, trace observed, 40 of 45).

Why this refutes wb-g1g.2 acceptance: B3 "neighbors beyond caps collapse to a counted remainder, never silently dropped" and the bead title's "missing relations never fabricated, incomplete-trace labeled". A trace labeled "observed" with an exact-claimed remainder while observed matching edges are dropped is a fabricated completeness claim, reachable through the intended consumer path (wb-6ze.24 computes the slice from ObservationProjection typed relations; production maxQuery is 40).

Suggested fix (red-first): falsifier first — maxQuery-40 projection with 45 matching edges under DEFAULT caps must yield remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace/relations-truncated (or an exact count of 35). Then either (a) adopt relationsPage {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied} once wb-6ze.27 lands (consumer adoption is explicitly excluded from wb-6ze.27's scope, so no other bead covers this) and treat truncated || limitApplied < requested as a full page, or (b) require/accept the projection's effective page cap from the caller and clamp the requested page to it. Existing behavior when the page is honored (rows.length >= page => atLeast + relations-truncated) is correct and must not regress; never weaken the delivered tests.

title: W14/VC-5: ObservationProjection reports relation-page truncation (new relationsPage returns {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied} beside a byte-identical relations(); truncated only when a further MATCHING edge exists past the page, never from index size; cross-scope keys stay empty with examined 0; read-only, no revision change; mirrors the query()/events() shapes); consumer adoption and hot files excluded
description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T10:40Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 24e6015, blobless clone, line anchors from `git show HEAD:<path>`): src/workbench/observation.ts:624 `relations(input: {scope; from?; to?; limit?}): Relation[]` clamps `limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? this.limits.maxQuery, this.limits.maxQuery)`, walks the outgoing/incoming/edgesByScope index and `break`s at the limit WITHOUT reporting it, while the sibling reads do report: `query()` (:704) returns `{nodes, examined, truncated}` and `events()` (:767) returns `{events, truncated, completeness}`. Production constructs the projection with maxQuery 40 (src/index.ts:2380, hot, not touched) and the W21 bench-only limits also pin maxQuery 40 (qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36), while consumers request up to 100 (attention.ts:73 RELATION_PAGE = 100; workflow-inspector.ts:92-93 limit:100) or 40 (timeline.ts relationLimit default). Every consumer therefore guesses: attention.ts:141 "relations() reports no truncation and the projection caps each page at its own maxQuery, which this selector cannot see" and re-reads pair by pair under a 2,000-read budget (:75, :155-166); timeline.ts:44 "relations() reports no truncation, so a page capped below this limit cannot be told from a complete one" and :363 flags `truncated.relations` only when `incoming.length >= relationLimit`; workflow-inspector.ts:94-98 "a projection configured below 100 truncates silently, which relations() cannot report". Gate record: the wb-6ze.1 gate accepted "production maxQuery 40 < 100 makes relation-page truncation undetectable through relations(), so (partial) and relations partial fire only at 100"; the wb-6ze.6 gate relayed worker follow-up (3) "relations() reports no truncation, so a reader page cap below relationLimit cannot be detected". The Sr. Engineer approved this bead: BOUNDARY.md 2026-10-15T10:23:58Z "Approved for groom: ... relations() truncation-visibility bead" and 10:32:20Z "the four worker follow-ups are groom-approved".

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): src/workbench/observation.ts plus ONE new test file.

- `export interface RelationPage { relations: Relation[]; examined: number; truncated: boolean; limitApplied: number }` and `relationsPage(input: {scope: ObservationScope; from?: string; to?: string; limit?: number}): RelationPage` on ObservationProjection. Same index selection as relations() (outgoing for `from`, incoming for `to`, edgesByScope otherwise), same scope-prefix guard, same exact from/to filters, same `Invalid relation query limit.` throw. `limitApplied = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery)`. `examined` counts edges visited. `truncated` is true iff at least one further MATCHING edge exists beyond the returned rows: the walk looks one matching edge past the limit and stops. It never derives truncation from an index bucket's size, because a bucket may hold edges the exact from/to filter excludes.
- `relations()` keeps its signature and return type; it shares the private walk so `relations(input)` deep-equals `relationsPage(input).relations` for every input (falsifier below).
- Cross-scope `from`/`to` keys (prefix mismatch) return `{relations: [], examined: 0, truncated: false, limitApplied}` exactly as relations() returns `[]` today; a cross-scope caller learns nothing about edge counts.
- Read-only: `revision`, `topologyRevision`, indexes, edges and `stats()` are unchanged by any number of calls; no retained state is added.
- Export RelationPage so attention.ts, timeline.ts, the topology slice and the inspector can adopt it in follow-ups (a sibling adoption bead for attention.ts + timeline.ts is filed blocked-by this bead in the same groom round).

Files: src/workbench/observation.ts (additive method + exported type), test/workbench-observation-relations-page.test.ts (new). test/workbench-observation.test.ts may gain additive cases; its existing cases stay untouched.

Out of scope: consumer adoption (attention.ts, timeline.ts in the sibling bead; src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts relationsFor() :86-98 belongs to the wb-6ze.16/.21/.23/.26 serialization chain; wb-g1g.2 topology slice and wb-752.2 observe reply builder are in flight), any change to maxQuery or production limits, src/index.ts or any other hot file, Pi tool registration.

Falsifiers (mutation proof, run on a scratch copy and tabled in the delivery note): M1 `truncated := rows.length >= limit` (exact-limit page with no remainder must stay false); M2 `truncated := bucket.size > limit` ignoring the from/to filter (must stay false when the surplus is filtered out); M3 cross-scope key reports `examined > 0` (must stay 0); M4 relations() stops sharing the walk and diverges from `.relations` (deep-equal loop goes red); M5 relationsPage mutates revision (read-only case goes red).

Event queries expose metadata and references without raw producer payloads. Source-qualified cursor retention loss is explicitly partial-gap." -- a projection constructed with {maxQuery: 2} holding 3 outgoing edges from key A answers relationsPage({scope, from: A, limit: 100}) with relations.length 2, truncated true, limitApplied 2; with exactly 2 edges truncated is false; under maxQuery 100 with limit 3 and 3 edges truncated is false and limitApplied 3; a property loop over limits 1..5 x edge counts 0..5 x {from, to, scope-wide} asserts truncated === (matching > relations.length) and relations(input) deep-equals relationsPage(input).relations.

A2 filter-aware, never fabricated from the index. docs/workbench/09 section "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "Store edge provenance with timestamp and source; Graph view styles each differently. Missing edges do not imply independence." and docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four-view viewport increment": "Missing edges, timestamps and evidence loaders are visible unknowns, never fabricated." -- with 5 edges A->C and 1 edge A->B, relationsPage({scope, from: A, to: B, limit: 1}) returns the single A->B row with truncated false (the 5 unmatched bucket entries create no truncation) and examined >= 1; every returned row carries kind and a copied provenance {source, observedAt?, nativeConfirmationRef?} and mutating a returned row never changes a later read.

A3 brute-force falsifier. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Matrix by subsystem" Observation row: positive proof "snapshots, dedup, cursor resume, provenance", negative control "event loss -> stale and unknown" -- over a seeded random edge set (200+ edges, 5 kinds, 2 scopes, duplicate from/to pairs) and 500+ random queries, truncated equals (referenceMatchingCount > relations.length) in every case, relations.length <= limitApplied, and the returned rows are the first limitApplied matching rows in index order (the same order relations() returns today).

A4 scope boundary. docs/workbench/09 section "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls." -- a from/to key of another workspace or principal yields {relations: [], examined: 0, truncated: false} and relations() yields []; a scope-wide page for scope B never includes a scope-A edge and reports truncation only from scope-B edges; the ownership edge of another scope is never counted toward truncation.

description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g1 round 15, run g1-r3; measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program 24e6015, BOUNDARY base 0fc3c86+; line anchors from `git show 24e6015:<path>`).

docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md section "Migration acceptance": "Headless or detached host doesn't require launching Pi's TUI process."; docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Install profile": "Separate: embedded Pi extension with local Claude SDK host; optional headless executor library/process for detached runs; optional Furnace ExecutorApp adapter (later); independently installed provider adapters."; docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "Pi remains the intelligence": "These services must also be usable without TUI to support tests and optional detached hosting." No test measures what the detached host actually loads. Reading the import statements at the tip: src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts (:11-27) imports node builtins, typescript, ../../workflow/runtime.js, ../capability-registry.js, ../claude-host.js, ../identity.js, the four provider adapters and ../redaction.js -- UI-free at the first level -- but src/workbench/claude-host.ts:18 imports ../workflow/saved.js, src/workflow/saved.ts:41-42 imports `getAgentDir` from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent" and ../memory.js, and src/memory.ts imports @earendil-works/pi-tui (git grep count 1). The "headless" host therefore transitively loads both Pi packages today as libraries. That is a caveat to RECORD, not a failure to assert: the spec sentence is about launching the TUI process, and a library load is not a TUI launch. qa/workbench/local-detached.sh is a process-lifecycle proof and makes no module-graph claim; `git grep -l pi-tui -- test/workbench-*.test.ts` hits only the inspector rendering tests. Without a census, a future convenience import (src/index.ts, src/ui/*, a pi-tui renderer) can silently turn the detached host into a Pi-TUI-dependent process and nobody will know.

Scope (measurement-only, src untouched, hot-file free):
- qa/workbench/headless-host-census.mjs (new runner): spawns `node --import <tracer>` (a tiny ESM module.register resolve hook recording every resolved specifier and url, or the loader mechanism the pinned Node supports) with stdin/stdout/stderr piped (no TTY) over dist/workbench/hosts/local-detached.js: imports the module, constructs createDetachedWorkflowHost({ backend: "deterministic", ... }) with an empty registry and no grants, calls validateScript on a trivial script, and exits. It emits a `workbench.headless-census/v1` receipt {utc, revision, node, closure (sorted, package-root-relative urls; node_modules reduced to package names with the first import chain), piPackages, uiModules, ttyFree, pass}. The runner never launches a Pi session, never opens a socket and never starts a detached host process (qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs owns that).
- test/workbench-headless-census.test.ts (new): red first over the receipt builder with a fixture closure; a frozen EXPECTED_PI_CLOSURE allowlist of Pi/TUI entries permitted today (exactly "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent" via src/workflow/saved.js and "@earendil-works/pi-tui" via src/memory.js, chains recorded) and EXPECTED_UI_MODULES = [] (no src/ui/*, no src/index.js); any unlisted Pi/UI entry fails naming the module and its chain; a recorded caveat that no longer appears also fails until the allowlist is trimmed in the same commit, so the caveat table never goes stale silently (wb-cax.8 exclusion rule, wb-cax.15 stale-row rule).
- forge.toml: one additive command for the runner (wb-cax.1 precedent), outside the default gate when it needs a built dist; the vitest guard runs inside the gate.

## 2026-10-15 14:53Z (system UTC) flywheel orchestrator — OWNER RULING F8 (wb-0kg.5 gate): ownership vs actionability for local-detached control
Host loss does NOT withdraw ownership confirmation — ownership is identity, not liveness (the invocation -> host-process edge survives host loss by design). But ACTIONABILITY requires LIVE confirmation: the control wiring re-reads the invocation's freshness at decision time, and a lost-host (freshness stale / observation unknown) invocation REFUSES the control action fail-closed with a reconcile pointer (the RECONCILE hint), never acting on a stale ownership edge. decideControl itself reads no freshness (control.ts:148-185), so this check belongs in the wiring (wb-cra) and the adapter must meet a lost host fail-closed (wb-0kg.6). Red-first cases: owned + live -> permitted path reachable; owned + host-lost -> refused with reconcile pointer; owned + unknown -> refused.

Pane rules to implement (literal reading of docs/10; the owner may re-rule pane assignment — record any ruling in the delivery note):
- width < 80 OR rows < 20: the existing single-column rendering, unchanged.

Each pane has its own row cap equal to the shared body height; rows past the cap end with the existing "… N more row(s)" notice (never silently dropped); pane widths split the inner width with the left pane never narrower than 40 columns.
- width >= 120 AND rows >= 20: three panes — left hierarchy (overview tree), center graph when state.view is overview or graph else timeline lanes, right details — when viable, meaning each pane keeps a minimum width of 36 columns after two separators; otherwise fall back to the two-pane rule. Pane widths are capped (no pane wider than 80 columns; surplus is left blank) and the total line count never exceeds rows.
- The header lines (title/status, view/count/follow, filter, focus, rule) span the full width above the panes; the key-hint line stays the last row.

title: W22-M/W06: bounded in-flight admission in CapabilityRegistry.invoke (one registry-wide maxInFlight from an exported constant, FIFO wait bounded by the existing deadline and caller signal, typed 'unavailable' admission refusal distinct from the transport deadline, provider never called for a refused request, slot held until the provider settles, never auto-retry, counts-only admission snapshot for telemetry); runtime, worker and index.ts untouched
description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T09:48Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 4ca6bd5; file lines from the rig checkout, unchanged at the tip): docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Runtime and host requirements" requires "Streaming bounded by max in-flight node calls, backend admission and configured quota." docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Registration and resolution" requires "Establish max input/output sizes, execution deadlines, memory/event quotas and secret redaction." and its section "Current experimental policy surface" records what exists: "The host registry bounds JSON depth, bytes and wait deadlines." Measured: src/workbench/capability-registry.ts CapabilityLimits carries only maxBytes, maxDepth and deadlineMs (lines 58-65, validated at 197-203); invoke() (line 253) applies the deadline timer and the caller signal and nothing else; the only concurrency-adjacent bound anywhere is src/workflow/runtime.ts:690 `const nodeCap = 1000`, a TOTAL node-call count per workflow, so a script's parallel() over hundreds of node() calls dispatches every call at once against the native providers (forge/furnace/hx/rf CLIs and SDK clients) with no admission and no quota. Store dedupe (bd list --status all, terms in-flight/inflight/admission/quota/concurren/backpressure): no bead covers it.

Scope (atomic): src/workbench/capability-registry.ts plus one new test file. One registry-wide bound, no per-capability table (the owner can add one later); no edits to src/workflow/runtime.ts, src/workflow/worker-source.ts or src/index.ts (runtime/index.ts are HOT; the worker needs nothing because admission lives host-side where every node(), curated Claude MCP tool and Pi tool path already calls registry.invoke/inspect).

Design to implement:
- CapabilityLimits.maxInFlight?: number, validated exactly like the existing limits (safe integer >= 1, else CapabilityError("validation", "Invalid capability limit maxInFlight.")).
- One exported constant CAPABILITY_MAX_IN_FLIGHT (proposed 32) as the default; tests read the constant, never a literal (wb-oon/wb-cax.8 single-carrier precedent).
- Admission applies to invoke mode and inspect mode alike. When inFlight >= maxInFlight the call WAITS in FIFO order for a slot; the wait is bounded by the SAME deadlineMs timer and the SAME caller signal the call already has (no second clock, no new option).
- A call still queued when its deadline fires is refused with CapabilityError("unavailable", ...) whose message names admission and the bound (e.g. "Capability <id> admission exhausted: <maxInFlight> in flight after <deadlineMs>ms."); this is deliberately distinct from the existing CapabilityError("transport", "... exceeded its deadline ...") that means the provider WAS called. A call cancelled while queued keeps the existing "transport" cancellation family. In both cases provider.invoke/inspect is never called for that request.
- A slot is held until the provider promise settles, not until the caller is answered: a hung provider stays counted in inFlight after its caller's deadline rejection, so saturation is visible rather than hidden (honest backpressure; docs/06: a deadline "does not establish producer rollback").
- No automatic retry of a refused or queued-then-cancelled call (docs/06 "No generic auto-retry").
- registry.admission(): Readonly<{maxInFlight; inFlight; peakInFlight; admitted; refused; cancelledWhileQueued}> as a frozen counts-only snapshot for wb-cax.13's "provider call outcomes" telemetry; no ids, no provider names, no payloads.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-registry-admission.test.ts fails before CapabilityLimits.maxInFlight exists. Base 4ca6bd5 or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1. Bound exists and is validated. docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Registration and resolution": "Establish max input/output sizes, execution deadlines, memory/event quotas and secret redaction." -> new CapabilityRegistry({maxInFlight: 0}), ({maxInFlight: 1.5}) and ({maxInFlight: -1}) throw CapabilityError category "validation" with message "Invalid capability limit maxInFlight." (the existing limit-validation path); a registry constructed without the option uses the exported constant CAPABILITY_MAX_IN_FLIGHT and registry.admission().maxInFlight equals that constant (the test imports the constant; no literal).

A2. FIFO wait, not refusal, while a slot will free. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Runtime and host requirements": "Streaming bounded by max in-flight node calls, backend admission and configured quota." -> with {maxInFlight: 1} and a provider whose invoke resolves only when the test releases it, three concurrent invoke() calls reach provider.invoke one at a time in request order (release #1 -> #2 enters; release #2 -> #3 enters); provider.invoke call count is exactly 1 until the first release; all three callers resolve with their validated values; admission() reports inFlight 0, peakInFlight 1, admitted 3, refused 0 afterwards.

A3. Typed admission refusal, distinct from the transport deadline, provider never called. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md section "Workbench core types" (NodeCallResult): `{ kind: "rejected"; category: "validation" | "authorization" | "unavailable"; diagnostic: string }` and docs/workbench/06 section "Current experimental policy surface": "A deadline stops the caller's wait; it does not establish producer rollback." -> with {maxInFlight: 1, deadlineMs: 50} and the first call held open, a second invoke() rejects with CapabilityError category "unavailable" whose message contains "admission" and the bound; the provider was called exactly once (never for the second request); the message differs from the existing transport-deadline text ("exceeded its deadline"); a third call issued after the first is released succeeds (the refusal left no stale queue state).

A4. Cancellation while queued. docs/workbench/06 section "InvocationContext": "cancellation signal for current wait" -> a queued call whose context.signal aborts rejects with CapabilityError category "transport" (the existing cancellation family), provider.invoke count unchanged, and admission().cancelledWhileQueued increments by one; the slot order of the remaining waiters is unchanged (the next waiter still enters when the running call settles).

A5. Slot held until the provider settles. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "State/event semantics" (via the registry's own deadline comment): a caller rejected by its transport deadline while the provider promise is still pending leaves admission().inFlight at 1 until the provider promise settles; a new call with {maxInFlight: 1} during that window is admission-refused (A3 path) rather than dispatched alongside the hung provider; after the provider settles inFlight returns to 0. Uncertain-effect semantics of the existing deadline path are unchanged (no new "uncertain-effect" category minted here).

A6. Inspect mode shares the bound. docs/workbench/06 section "Optional inspect/observe" -> registry inspect-mode calls occupy the same slots as invoke-mode calls (one held inspect blocks a second invoke under {maxInFlight: 1} and vice versa), proven both directions.

A7. Never auto-retry. docs/workbench/06 section "Registration and resolution": "No generic auto-retry; producer-specific adapters alone may reconcile native logical identities." -> after an admission refusal or a queued cancellation the provider is never invoked later for that request (count asserted after all other calls settle and after one macrotask turn).

A8. Telemetry snapshot is counts only. docs/workbench/17 section "Operations telemetry": "Report actual: ... provider call outcomes ..." and "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." -> admission() returns an Object.isFrozen snapshot with exactly the keys maxInFlight, inFlight, peakInFlight, admitted, refused, cancelledWhileQueued, all safe integers; serialized it contains no capability id, provider name, input or output text (asserted against a fixture whose capability id and payload carry a unique marker).

A9. No production behaviour change elsewhere: src diff touches only src/workbench/capability-registry.ts; all existing registry/security/node-contract/curated-tool suites pass unchanged; biome clean; no any; no inline imports; no hot file touched.

title: W22-K/docs-17: pure operations-telemetry report over the projection and supplied counters (active workflows with last-known-running+stale sub-count, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag p50/p95 + clock caveat, dropped/late observations, projection size, visible rows, render p95, memory, SDK tokens, evidence coverage, ambiguous effects; each metric measured-with-source or unknown-with-reason, never default zero; counts and sanitized provider names only); wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at trunk 0ef5aeb, origin/workbench/implementation-program): docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Operations telemetry" requires "Report actual: active workflows, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag, dropped/late observations, projection size, number of visible rows, UI render p95, memory, token use from SDK, native evidence coverage and ambiguous external effects. Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." grep -rni 'telemetry' src/ returns one OpenTelemetry comment (src/index.ts:714); no module aggregates any of these twelve quantities. The inputs exist: ObservationProjection exposes query() (src/workbench/observation.ts:477), events() (:540, completeness "complete" | "partial-gap") and stats() (:558 -> {nodes, events, edges}); ObservedNode carries kind, presentation.statusTone, freshness, sourceConnectionState, evidenceRefs and nativeRef (:56-76); ObservationEvent carries sourceTimestamp? and observedAt (:12-28); ingest() returns "applied" | "duplicate" | "out-of-order" (:261) but retains no counters; CapabilityErrorCategory (src/workbench/capability-registry.ts:39) names the provider outcome categories; the Claude host computes per-call token usage (src/workbench/claude-host.ts:83-89) but publishes no aggregate. wb-6ze.4 (landed a4cd2cf) set the pattern this bead follows: a pure, caller-clocked, bounded selector over one projection page with measured-vs-unknown labelling. wb-752.2 (in progress) builds the workflow_observe reply and may surface this report later; wb-cax.10 (owner-held) covers the other docs/17 residual (lazy init). No bead covers operations telemetry.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/telemetry.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-telemetry.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const TELEMETRY_CONTRACT = "workbench.telemetry/v1"; export const TELEMETRY_CLOCK_CAVEAT (event lag compares producer sourceTimestamp with observedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled).
- export type TelemetryMetric<T> = { state: "measured"; value: T; source: "projection" | "supplied" } | { state: "unknown"; reason: "not-supplied" | "invalid-supplied" | "no-source-timestamps" | "no-events" }.
- export interface SuppliedCounters { providerCallOutcomes?: Readonly<Partial<Record<"returned" | CapabilityErrorCategory, number>>>; droppedObservations?: number; lateObservations?: number; visibleRows?: number; renderP95Ms?: number; heapUsedBytes?: number; sdkTokens?: number; claudeSessions?: number; uncertainEffects?: number } -- the host/dialog counts these (ingest results, provider outcomes, render timings, SDK usage) and passes them in; this bead defines the shape only.
- export function buildOperationsTelemetry(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "events" | "stats">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId?: string; now: string; limit?: number (default 100, max 100); eventLimit?: number (default 200, max 1000); supplied?: SuppliedCounters }): OperationsTelemetry -- a frozen report { contract; now; examined: { nodes; truncated; events; eventsTruncated; completeness: "complete" | "partial-gap" }; activeWorkflows: TelemetryMetric<{ active: number; lastKnownRunningStale: number }>; claudeSdkSessions: TelemetryMetric<number> (projection count of nodes with nativeRef.provider "claude-agent-sdk" and type "session"; a supplied claudeSessions is reported beside it with source "supplied", never merged); providerCallOutcomes: TelemetryMetric<Record<string, number>>; eventLag: TelemetryMetric<{ p50Ms; p95Ms; samples; unmeasured; providers: string[]; caveat: string }>; droppedObservations, lateObservations: TelemetryMetric<number>; projectionSize: TelemetryMetric<{ nodes; events; edges }>; visibleRows, renderP95Ms, heapUsedBytes, sdkTokens, uncertainEffects: TelemetryMetric<number>; nativeEvidenceCoverage: TelemetryMetric<{ withEvidence: number; examined: number }> }.
- Rules: projection-derived metrics come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit}) page and ONE bounded projection.events({scope, limit: eventLimit}) read; truncated and partial-gap flags are propagated into examined. activeWorkflows.active counts nodes with kind "workflow" and statusTone "active"; lastKnownRunningStale counts those with freshness !== "current" or sourceConnectionState "disconnected" (docs/09 § "Freshness and ambiguity" nuance). eventLag samples are observedAt minus sourceTimestamp in ms for events carrying both (negative samples clamp to 0 and are counted in unmeasured, as are events without sourceTimestamp); p50/p95 by nearest-rank over the sorted samples; providers = sorted distinct event.source.provider. Supplied metrics are measured only when the supplied value is a finite non-negative number (for the outcome record: every value finite non-negative), else unknown "not-supplied" / "invalid-supplied"; the report never defaults an absent counter to 0. now is the caller's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now); the projection is never mutated.
- Redaction: the report contains no node titles, status text, evidence ref strings, prompts, tool bodies or payload refs -- counts and provider names only; provider names pass redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText (src/workbench/redaction.ts) and are capped at 64 chars; JSON.stringify(report) stays under 8 KiB for the maximum page and the test asserts it.

Out of scope: host-side counting (ingest-result counters, provider outcome counters, render timings, SDK usage aggregation live in src/index.ts, the dialog and hosts -- HOT or owner wiring; this bead defines SuppliedCounters only), inspector header or workflow_observe surfacing (wb-752.2), process.memoryUsage or any node:* read inside the module, docs or TRACEABILITY edits.

Specs: docs/workbench/17 (Operations telemetry; Error and degradation policy "Offline observation -> last-known state visibly stale; no fake terminal completion."), docs/workbench/09 (Observation event envelope; Freshness and ambiguity; Aggregates and profiling; Data retention and privacy), docs/workbench/13 (Agent execution contracts "no invented zeros or fake IDs"), docs/workbench/12 (Credential boundaries), docs/workbench/15 W22.
acceptance_criteria:
All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, base 0ef5aeb or later per BOUNDARY.md).
1. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Operations telemetry": "Report actual: active workflows, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag, dropped/late observations, projection size, number of visible rows, UI render p95, memory, token use from SDK, native evidence coverage and ambiguous external effects." -> the report type has exactly these twelve metric fields (plus contract, now, examined); a fixture projection with 3 workflow nodes (2 active, 1 success) and 2 "claude-agent-sdk"/"session" nodes yields activeWorkflows {active:2, lastKnownRunningStale:0}, claudeSdkSessions 2 and projectionSize equal to projection.stats(); every field is either {state:"measured", value, source} or {state:"unknown", reason} (type-level exhaustiveness plus a runtime walk over the report).
2. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Agent execution contracts": "If the installed SDK lacks a field, omit it; no invented zeros or fake IDs." -> with supplied undefined, providerCallOutcomes, droppedObservations, lateObservations, visibleRows, renderP95Ms, heapUsedBytes, sdkTokens and uncertainEffects are all {state:"unknown", reason:"not-supplied"}; JSON.stringify(report) contains no "value":0 for those fields; a supplied NaN, -1 or Infinity yields "invalid-supplied"; a supplied {returned:4, transport:1, "uncertain-effect":1} is measured with source "supplied" and every key preserved.
3. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Observation event envelope (proposal)": "SourceTimestamp does not establish a total order across providers." -> eventLag over events from providers "forge" and "furnace" reports samples, p50Ms, p95Ms, providers ["forge","furnace"] and caveat === TELEMETRY_CLOCK_CAVEAT; events without sourceTimestamp are counted in unmeasured and never sampled; a window with zero timestamped events is {state:"unknown", reason:"no-source-timestamps"} ("no-events" when the window is empty); an events() read returning completeness "partial-gap" sets examined.completeness "partial-gap".
4. docs/workbench/09 § "Freshness and ambiguity": "A disconnected Furnace event stream must not make a previously RUNNING node permanently authoritative RUNNING; it becomes last-known-running + stale. Pi tool summaries must communicate that nuance." -> after projection.disconnect("furnace") an active furnace workflow node is counted in both active and lastKnownRunningStale; after a real refresh() snapshot restores the node, lastKnownRunningStale returns to 0 while active is unchanged; reconnect() alone does not clear it.
5. docs/workbench/17 § "Operations telemetry": "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." with docs/workbench/09 § "Data retention and privacy": "Avoid raw prompts/tool bodies by default; store reference/short redacted preview" and docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages." -> with node titles "Bearer abc123 secret", status text containing "api_key":"xyz" and evidenceRefs ["claude-message:0000"], JSON.stringify(report) contains none of "Bearer", "abc123", "xyz", "api_key" or "claude-message"; a provider name "fur\x1b[31mnace​" appears sanitized; JSON.stringify(report).length < 8192 for a 100-node/1000-event page.
6. docs/workbench/09 § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics." -> nativeEvidenceCoverage reports {withEvidence, examined} as two counts (no ratio or percentage is invented); a query page capped at limit 100 over 150 nodes reports examined.truncated true and the test asserts the coverage counts describe the examined page, not the projection.
7. Purity: buildOperationsTelemetry never calls Date.now (static grep of the module plus a Date.now spy), never mutates the projection (stats() and query() results identical before and after), returns deep-frozen output (Object.isFrozen on every nested object), and the module's import specifiers are limited to ./observation.js, ./capability-registry.js and ./redaction.js (static assertion).
