- export const EVIDENCE_LOADER_ROWS: frozen table of exactly three rows {provider, requiredGrant, refKind}: {"claude-agent-sdk", "claude:transcript", "claude-message:<uuid>"}, {"furnace", "furnace:inspect", "native Attempt id listed on the owning run node"}, {"forge", "forge:inspect", "forge-operation:<operation_id>"} -- the docs/20 § "Producer mapping" table and nothing else.
- export function createEvidenceLoaders(input: { grants: () => readonly string[]; readers: { claude?: <landed claude-evidence.ts read function>; furnace?: <landed furnace-evidence.ts read function>; forge?: <landed forge-evidence.ts read function> }; owningFreshness: (scope: ObservationScope, nativeRef: NativeRef) => ObservedNode["freshness"] | "disconnected" | undefined }): readonly EvidenceLoader[]. Read EvidenceLoader/EvidenceContent/EvidenceRequest from the landed src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (wb-g1g.1) and the reader signatures from the landed reader modules at claim time; never re-declare or re-implement either.
- Layer 1: a loader is constructed only when input.grants() (read once at construction) contains the row's requiredGrant as an exact string AND the matching reader is supplied; malformed or unknown grant entries are ignored (deny). Layer 2: every load(request) re-reads input.grants() and throws CapabilityError("authorization", ...) before touching the reader when the exact grant is absent.
- Routing: loader.provider equals the row provider; canLoad(ref) is the row's shape check only (uuid shape for claude-message, validated operation id for forge-operation, the furnace reader's own Attempt-id predicate); load(request) throws CapabilityError("validation") when request.nativeRef.provider !== loader.provider or !canLoad(request.evidenceRef) -- the store routes provider-first, the loader never guesses.
- Assembly: load returns the full EvidenceContent (docs/20 ruling 1): kind, provider, capturedAt, bytes, truncated, preview (the reader's lines passed through the idempotent shared sanitizers redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText from src/workbench/redaction.ts; no new lines, no raw payload retained), sourceBasis only when digest-shaped (sha256:<64 hex> or the identity digest shape), otherwise omitted; freshness "stale" when owningFreshness reports stale, unknown, disconnected or undefined, "current" only for "current"; producerReceipt passed through when the reader supplies one. Reader failures propagate as CapabilityError with the reader's category (transport/authorization/unavailable/validation), never converted into a loaded entry; each loader exposes freshnessOf(request) so the store can label a transport failure against a disconnected source as transport plus stale.
- Anything else (hyperunix, reactivefiber, beads, unknown providers): no loader is produced, so the store yields unavailable: no-loader; the factory never fabricates a loader or a preview.
- Frozen outputs; no Date.now (capturedAt comes from the reader); no SDK imports; node:* imports only if the landed readers require them.

Out of scope: src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (wb-g1g.1 owns it), the three reader modules (wb-6ze.8/.10/.11 own them), EvidenceStore construction and the load-evidence/abortAll dialog wiring (owner's wiring slice in src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts -- HOT), src/index.ts (HOT), hosts, grant settings parsing, any live SDK tier.

A loader constructed under a grant whose grants() later returns without it rejects load with CapabilityError category "authorization" and the reader spy records zero calls; "claude:transcript " (trailing space), "CLAUDE:TRANSCRIPT" and "claude:*" never satisfy the check (docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Authorization design": "Treat unknown permission data as deny.").
2. docs/workbench/20 § "Types": "`nativeRef` is required because evidence ref strings are not globally namespaced; producer routing keys off `nativeRef.provider` first, with `canLoad(evidenceRef)` as a shape check inside that producer only." and § "Owner rulings on the design conflicts" 3: "Loaders take the full request, not a bare ref; routing is provider-first." -> each loader's canLoad accepts exactly its row's ref shape and rejects the other two rows' shapes; load with request.nativeRef.provider "forge" on the claude loader rejects with category "validation" and calls no reader; the test enumerates all nine provider x ref-shape pairs and exactly three delegate to a reader.
3. docs/workbench/20 § "Producer mapping": rows "claude-agent-sdk session | `claude-message:<uuid>` | ... | `claude:transcript`", "furnace run | native Attempt id listed on the owning run node | ... | `furnace:inspect`", "forge operation | `forge-operation:<operation_id>` | ... | `forge:inspect`", "anything else | — | `unavailable: no-loader`, a visible unknown | —" -> EVIDENCE_LOADER_ROWS deep-equals exactly those three rows (a mutation test appending a fourth "hyperunix" row fails the pinned-table assertion); no loader is ever produced for a provider outside the table even when a grant such as "hyperunix:inspect" is present.
4. docs/workbench/20 § "Owner rulings" 1: "`loaded` equals the full `EvidenceContent` (kind, sourceBasis, freshness included)." and § "Types": "`sourceBasis` accepts digest-shaped values only." -> a reader result carrying sourceBasis "sha256:" + 64 hex is passed through; "main", "/tmp/x" and "sha256:abc" are omitted (never defaulted, never truncated into a fake digest); bytes, truncated, capturedAt and producerReceipt are copied from the reader, not recomputed; preview lines equal the reader's lines after the idempotent sanitizers and the factory adds no line (docs/20 ruling 2: "The double redaction in the sanitizer order is deliberate and idempotent." -- a reader line containing "\x1b[31m", U+202E or U+200B comes out stripped; an already-sanitized line comes out byte-identical).
5. docs/workbench/20 § "Refusal and freshness rules": "Stale or disconnected owning nodes label loaded evidence stale; a failed read against a disconnected source is transport plus stale. A loaded entry never upgrades projection freshness and never changes node status text or tone. Transport success never implies verification." -> owningFreshness "stale", "unknown", "disconnected" or undefined yields freshness "stale"; only "current" yields "current"; a reader CapabilityError("transport") propagates with the same category and loader.freshnessOf(request) reports "stale" for the disconnected owner; a forge reader result whose domain verdict is failed or partial is returned as its own kind/status, and the string "verified" appears nowhere in the module source nor in any emitted content under the fixture.
6. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" (Details): "Large content loaded only on focus." -> createEvidenceLoaders calls no reader (spy count 0 after construction); only load() delegates, exactly once per call.
7. Negative controls: a request whose scope differs from the owning node's scope is rejected "authorization" without a reader call; the module never imports an SDK or node:child_process (static assertion on import specifiers); a request for a provider with no row (e.g. "hyperunix") finds no loader in the returned array (the store renders no-loader) and the factory exposes no fallback path.

description:
Gap: docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Release checklist" item 8 requires "80x24, 120x40 and resize/SSH terminal tests pass." No deterministic conformance tier asserts rendering correctness at those geometries: wb-9x5.1 TIMES navigation/layout at 80x24/120x40/ASCII/resize but asserts no width, reflow or readability invariants, and wb-6ze.15 is the separate LIVE pty acceptance (blocked). Scope (atomic, test-only, src untouched, in the default gate):
- test/workbench-terminal-geometry.test.ts (new): drive the exported workflow card and four-view inspector renderers (the same compiled-surface entry points wb-9x5.1 benches) over a small deterministic fixture containing long Unicode/CJK/combining titles, zero-width characters and adversarial ANSI/OSC input.
- Geometry invariants at 80x24 and 120x40: every emitted line fits the column budget display-width aware (CJK wide cells, combining marks, zero-width stripped per the landed sanitizer rules); row count never exceeds the viewport; truncation is explicit, never silent overflow.
- Resize reflow: 120x40 -> 80x24 -> 120x40 mid-session re-render leaves no stale rows or artifacts, keeps the selection valid, and is idempotent for an unchanged model.
- SSH/dumb tier: the ASCII/dumb-TERM rendering path emits no raw ANSI/OSC control sequences and stays readable; adversarial input is neutralized via the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (standing invariant).
- No timing claims (wb-9x5.1 owns timing); no live pty (wb-6ze.15 owns the live check); no src/ edits of any kind.

description:

Gap (measured at rig HEAD, branch workbench/implementation-program, origin 40a031a; BOUNDARY base 9bea995+): docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md § "Compatibility feature control" requires "Tests must run in both upstream/Pi and new/Claude workbench modes until a documented deprecation is approved", and docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Test classes" class B defines the compatibility golden as "actual upstream Claude-compatible scripts in examples/workflows plus docs/workflows.md semantics; compare stable result shape, phase grouping, parallel/pipeline ordering contract, failures, metadata, nested workflow resolution, JSON schema and budget behavior". Today every golden runs under ONE backend: test/workflow-examples.test.ts drives all five examples/workflows/*.js (compose, fan-out-audit, gated-fix, review-panel, structured-findings, plus lib/count-child.js) through runWorkflow({script, host}) with a hand-built stub WorkflowHost (stubHost(), :74-110), and test/workflow-claude-code-compat.test.ts likewise builds its own WorkflowHost (:40, :60). Nothing runs those scripts through createClaudeWorkflowHost (src/workbench/claude-host.ts:95), whose ClaudeWorkflowHostOptions.query?: ClaudeQuery (claude-host.ts:24, :41) is the injectable SDK seam; the only golden-adjacent mention of workflowAgentBackend is settings parsing (test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts:228-231). wb-a2g.2 (landed 9c1c42f) shipped test/helpers/claude-sdk-stream.ts (FakeClaudeSdk, FakeSdkCall, sdkInit, sdkAssistantText, sdkAssistantToolUse, sdkResultSuccess, sdkSuccess), which scripts deterministic SDK message streams for exactly this seam. wb-cax.4 (open) pins the registered surface per mode and wb-cax.5 (open) covers the degradation lines; neither executes the goldens under the Claude backend.

Scope (atomic, test-only, hot-file free; src/ untouched): ONE new test file test/workflow-examples-claude-backend.test.ts plus at most ONE new helper test/helpers/golden-backends.ts (a shared label->answer table so both hosts answer identically). For every examples/workflows/*.js (glob-driven, same discovery as workflow-examples.test.ts) and lib/count-child.js, run the unmodified script twice: (A) the upstream stub WorkflowHost over the answer table; (B) a host from createClaudeWorkflowHost({cwd, model: 'fixture-model', tools: [], query: fixture, ...}) whose fixture ClaudeQuery is built from test/helpers/claude-sdk-stream.ts and answers from the same table (JSON text for schema-bearing calls, prose otherwise) with a distinct fake native session id per call. Normalize both results (status; error class/message prefix; value JSON with arrays sorted only where the example's own contract is order-insensitive; agentCount / number of agent() calls; phase grouping through the existing src/workflow/progress.ts projector; metadata keys; nested resolution of lib/count-child.js; schema-rejection class; budget-exhaustion class) and assert deep equality A == B. Negative controls: (1) a spy standing in for the legacy Pi spawn path records zero calls under (B); (2) an agent() call with an unsupported option key fails at the call under BOTH backends with the same error class; (3) the SDK fixture records exactly one query per agent() call, each with a distinct session id, so a backend that batched, re-ran or skipped a call fails; (4) one deliberately divergent fixture answer makes the equivalence assertion fail (mutation proof run once, documented). No live model, no network, no TTY.

Out of scope: src/ changes of any kind (if the equivalence reveals a genuine backend divergence, file a separate bead carrying the normalized diff instead of adjusting the test or the normalizer); docs edits; test/workflow-examples.test.ts, test/workflow-claude-code-compat.test.ts and test/helpers/claude-sdk-stream.ts stay byte-identical; hot files src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts, src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts, test/workbench-security-workflow.test.ts untouched.

Files: test/workflow-examples-claude-backend.test.ts (new), test/helpers/golden-backends.ts (new, optional). Specs: docs/workbench/16 (Compatibility feature control; Migration acceptance), docs/workbench/14 (Test classes B; Matrix by subsystem rows "Claude SDK host" and "Legacy scripts"; Truth labels and release gates), docs/workbench/15 (VC-1 "legacy script fixtures unchanged"; W22 "reproducible Forge gate"), docs/workbench/02 WB-003.

4. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Matrix by subsystem", row Legacy scripts: "unchanged script executes with same semantics | unsupported option fails at call" -> a script passing an unknown agent() option key fails at the call under both backends with the same error class and a message naming the key; example sources are read from examples/workflows byte-for-byte (no rewriting, no injected globals).

6. Mutation proof: with one label's fixture answer deliberately changed for the Claude backend only, criterion 2's equivalence assertion fails for the affected example and passes for the others (run once, command id recorded in the bead notes or the machine ledger, then reverted).

Red-first: test/workbench-execute.test.ts fails before src/workbench/execute.ts exists. Base 23404b4 or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

E1. Tool shape. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_execute(definitionRef,input,hostMode,policy?): authorized launch; returns logical invocation and native references, not false completion." -> decideExecute accepts exactly {definitionRef, input, hostMode, policy?}; the reply built from an injected launch outcome carries the logical invocation reference and the native references the launch reported, and a status that is launch-level only (e.g. accepted/launched/refused); asserting a completed/successful terminal state from a launch outcome is impossible by construction (falsifier test).
E2. Immutable digest. docs/workbench/11 section "Operator actions versus designer edits": "Design-time edits occur against versioned source; execution against immutable digest." -> a definitionRef that is not digest-pinned is refused with a typed diagnostic before any grant check consumes it.
E3. Exact execute authority. docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md: "Registered descriptors do not grant access." and "Catalog discovery independently requires exact `discover:<capabilityId>`." plus docs/workbench/02 WB-034: "list/inspect never grant invoke." -> admission requires one exact execute-authority grant distinct from workbench:design, workbench:observe and every discover:/inspect: grant; proven both ways (grant present admits, grant absent refuses typed); a grant set holding only discover:/inspect:/design/observe grants NEVER admits (falsifier).
E4. No node-permission leakage. docs/workbench/06: "Invocation requires every explicit producer permission in the descriptor." -> the reply never claims or implies node-level capability permissions; it echoes the policy input verbatim-bounded and leaves per-node admission to the host registry seam.
E5. hostMode allowlist. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Install profile" separates "embedded Pi extension with local Claude SDK host" from "optional headless executor library/process for detached runs" -> hostMode is a closed allowlist (embedded, detached); an unknown hostMode is a typed refusal, never a guessed default.
E6. Sanitized bounded reply. Every string in the reply routes through the shared sanitizers (src/workbench/redaction.ts) and the reply is byte-capped with a visible truncation marker; raw launch payloads are never retained.
E7. Purity. The module performs no I/O, imports no SDK and never invokes the registry; vitest covers refusal and admission paths; biome clean; no any; no inline imports; no existing test weakened.

Scope (atomic, I/O only through the injected registry, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/forge-evidence.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-forge-evidence.test.ts; register and wire nothing; do not edit src/workbench/native-evidence.ts, src/workbench/forge-observer.ts, src/workbench/providers/forge.ts, src/workbench/capability-registry.ts, src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (does not exist yet; wb-g1g.1), src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts or src/index.ts. The module never imports @forge/sdk or node:*; tests use CapabilityRegistry + registerForgeGateStatus with a fixture ForgeReadClient (the test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts SOURCE shape).

• export const FORGE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT = 'workbench.forge-evidence/v1'; export const FORGE_READ_CAPABILITY = 'forge.gate.status'.
• export interface ForgeEvidenceRequest { registry: Pick<CapabilityRegistry,'invoke'>; grants: () => readonly string[] (the LIVE grant set, re-read per call and handed to the registry, which performs the exact forge:inspect check); principal?: { id: string; role?: string }; scope: ObservationScope; owningWorkspaceNode: { nativeRef: NativeRef; evidenceRefs: readonly string[] } (the projection node the ref was listed on; its nativeRef.scope is the gate.status target); evidenceRef: string; maxBytes: number (1..65536); maxLines: number (1..200); timeoutMs: number (1..2147483647); signal: AbortSignal; capturedAt: () => string (injected clock; the module never calls Date.now) }.
• export interface ForgeEvidenceContent { contract: typeof FORGE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT; kind: 'forge.operation.gate-status'; provider: 'forge'; nativeRef: NativeRef ({provider:'forge', type:'operation', id: requestedOperationId, scope: target}); capturedAt; bytes: number (UTF-8 byte length of JSON.stringify of the reading's source); truncated: boolean (preview lines dropped by maxLines, or bytes > maxBytes); preview: readonly string[] — line 1 'operation <requested> · read as operation <readId|none> (same operation|different operation: current re-read of the same target)', line 2 the workspace snapshot statusText that forgeGateTopology produced (for example 'success · FORGE_OK · verification indeterminate'), then one 'package <ref>: <package statusText>' line per package snapshot, bounded by maxLines, plus a final '… truncated (budget)' line whenever truncated; every line through redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText then a local zero-width strip of U+200B-U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF, max 200 characters; domainStatus: { status?: string; verdict?: string; reasonCode: string; qualifier: 'current gate failed' | 'current gate passed' | 'verification indeterminate' } quoted from the native source and from forgeGateTopology's workspace snapshot (single-sourced; this module never re-derives a verdict); sourceBasis?: string (present only when nativeEvidence(...).sourceBasis is, i.e. digest-shaped by construction, never a directory); producerReceipt: { requestedOperationId: string; readOperationId: string | null; sameOperation: boolean; protocolMethod: 'gate.status'; packages: number; diagnostics: readonly string[] (forgeGateTopology diagnostics, each sanitized and <= 200 characters) }; freshness: 'current' } — no verified, statusTone, tone or outcome field anywhere.
• export async function readForgeOperationEvidence(request: ForgeEvidenceRequest): Promise<ForgeEvidenceContent> — preconditions before any invoke (each a CapabilityError, registry never called): scope.workspace, scope.principal non-empty displayable strings (stripUnsafeText(value) === value, <= 256 bytes) else 'validation'; owningWorkspaceNode.nativeRef must be {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id:'workspace', scope: target} with target a non-empty displayable string of at most 4096 characters, else 'authorization' ("evidence ref is not listed on a Forge gate-status workspace node of this scope"; a package node {id: pkg.ref} is refused because forge-observer lists forge-operation refs on the workspace node only); evidenceRef absent from owningWorkspaceNode.evidenceRefs -> 'authorization'; evidenceRef not matching /^forge-operation:(\S{1,256})$/ with stripUnsafeText(id) === id -> 'validation'; budgets out of range -> 'validation'; signal already aborted -> 'transport' ("Forge evidence read cancelled before launch"). Exactly one registry.invoke('forge.gate.status', {target}, context) call where context carries grants: grants(), signal: request.signal, workspace: scope.workspace and the optional principal (the remaining InvocationContext fields come from the request with no fabricated identity; see capability-registry.ts:20-34), raced against request.signal and timeoutMs (abort or timeout -> 'transport'; the invoke promise is abandoned, never awaited further). A CapabilityError thrown by the registry (for example 'authorization' when forge:inspect is missing) is rethrown with the SAME category and its message passed through redactWorkbenchText capped at 200 characters; any other thrown error becomes CapabilityError('unavailable', redacted preview). Reading validation: nativeEvidence('forge.gate.status', reading).provider !== 'forge' -> 'unavailable' ("reading is not the forge.gate.status/v1 contract"); when source.data.workspace_context.root is a string and differs from target -> 'authorization' ("native read answered for another workspace"); forgeGateTopology(reading, {scope, target, capturedAt, observedAt: capturedAt}) is called exactly once and any CapabilityError it throws is rethrown as 'unavailable' ("malformed native gate.status shape: <sanitized message>"); readOperationId = nativeEvidence(...).nativeId ?? null; sameOperation = readOperationId === requestedOperationId. The content never retains the reading: no field named source, raw, data, packages (as an array), envelope or payload.
• Zero control or write verbs: the module invokes no capability id other than 'forge.gate.status' (a registry with a decoy registered write capability proves it is never invoked) and imports only ./capability-registry.js (CapabilityError, type CapabilityRegistry, type JsonValue), ./forge-observer.js (forgeGateTopology), ./native-evidence.js (nativeEvidence), ./observation.js (types) and ./redaction.js; it contains none of 'node:', '@forge/sdk', 'ServerConnection', 'process.', 'Date.now', 'Math.random', 'import('.

In the tree, src/index.ts:2479-2481 registerWorkbenchTools registers the seven workbench tools (workbench_catalog :2483, workflow_validate :2494, workflow_catalog :2513, workflow_compare :2527, furnace_observe :2550, workflow_detached :2573, workflow_observe :2594) from session_start only when sourceSettings(ctx)?.workflowAgentBackend === "claude", guarded once per process by workbenchToolsRegistered; the legacy Agent tool registers at activation (:2368-2369) and SubagentWorkflow only when isWorkflowsEnabled() (:2995); the single command is "agents" (:4382). test/workflow-tool.test.ts § "collisions with another extension" covers the legacy name against FOREIGN extensions and test/workbench-security-pi-tools.test.ts covers per-tool denials, but no test pins the registered surface per mode, proves the reload guard, or proves that grants leave the registered surface unchanged (grep over test/ for tools.keys(), registerTool call counts or workbenchToolsRegistered: none). A quietly duplicated, renamed or unconditionally registered tool, or a legacy definition that changes under the Claude backend, would pass the gate today.

Scope (atomic, test-only, src/ byte-identical, hot-file free): ONE new test file test/workbench-surface-census.test.ts built on test/helpers/boot-extension.ts (makePi, ctx, hermeticDir) that boots the REAL extension (src/index.ts default export) under four hermetic settings and fires session_start: (A) settings without a workbench key; (B) workbench {workflowAgentBackend:'pi'}; (C) workbench {workflowAgentBackend:'claude', capabilityGrants: []}; (D) workbench {workflowAgentBackend:'claude', capabilityGrants: ['workbench:design','workbench:observe','furnace:inspect','forge:inspect','claude:transcript','discover:forge.gate.status','invoke:forge.gate.status']}. The test pins, as literal sorted arrays measured at the base SHA (the measuring command and SHA recorded in a header comment), LEGACY_TOOLS (mode A tool names), WORKBENCH_TOOLS (the seven above), COMMANDS (['agents']) and FLAGS (registeredFlags keys), and asserts: sorted(tools of A) equals LEGACY_TOOLS; B equals A; C equals LEGACY_TOOLS ∪ WORKBENCH_TOOLS exactly (no extra, no missing); D equals C; LEGACY_TOOLS ∩ WORKBENCH_TOOLS is empty and no workbench name differs from a legacy name only by case or underscore/hyphen; registerTool mock call count equals tools.size in every mode (no name registered twice) and registerCommand call count equals commands.size; firing session_start a second time on the same booted pi (reload) adds zero registerTool and zero registerCommand calls in every mode; a stable projection of each legacy tool definition (name, description, parameters JSON, every non-function key) deep-equals between A and C and between C and D; commands and flag keys are identical across A-D; with settings {workflowsEnabled:false} under C, SubagentWorkflow is absent and the remaining surface is pinned as measured. Mutation proof (recorded in the closure receipt, run against a scratch copy of the tree, never in the candidate branch): M1 register workflow_observe a second time, M2 drop the workflowAgentBackend === "claude" condition at index.ts:2480, M3 drop the workbenchToolsRegistered guard, M4 rename SubagentWorkflow under the claude branch only — each mutant must fail the census while the unmutated tree passes.

Out of scope: any src/ edit (a measured violation is recorded as a finding and the bead returns blocked; the fix is separate work), registering new tools (wb-752.2 / wb-69g.2 registration beads update the pinned WORKBENCH_TOOLS literal in the same change, a one-line edit), docs/TRACEABILITY.md edits, the 14 pre-existing wiring tests (left verbatim), and live providers (every mode boots with mocked SDKs or none; no network).
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, a650133 or later). Measurement-only: src/ byte-identical in the candidate branch.

1. docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md § "Migration acceptance": "Existing upstream Pi agent workflows, script saved paths and UI work after extension reload. Claude Workbench mode can run and observe real Claude SDK agents; no accidental duplication of tools or permission escalation." -> in each of modes A-D the registerTool mock call count equals the number of distinct registered tool names and registerCommand call count equals the number of distinct commands; firing the recorded session_start handler a second time on the same booted pi adds zero registerTool and zero registerCommand calls in every mode; mode C's tool-name set equals exactly LEGACY_TOOLS ∪ WORKBENCH_TOOLS where WORKBENCH_TOOLS is the pinned literal ['furnace_observe','workbench_catalog','workflow_catalog','workflow_compare','workflow_detached','workflow_observe','workflow_validate'].
2. docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md § "Compatibility feature control": "Tests must run in both upstream/Pi and new/Claude workbench modes until a documented deprecation is approved." and "Maintain existing Workflow/SubagentWorkflow collision detection and dialog/menu semantics." -> modes A (no workbench key) and B (workflowAgentBackend 'pi') register identical tool-name sets, identical commands and identical flag keys, equal to the pinned LEGACY_TOOLS measured at the base SHA named in the test header; the stable projection (name, description, parameters JSON and every non-function key) of every legacy tool deep-equals between A and C; LEGACY_TOOLS contains 'SubagentWorkflow' and the Agent tool name, and no workbench name equals a legacy name, or differs from one only by case or by underscore versus hyphen.
3. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-011: "The existing workflow tool remains available in Pi without collision or competing shadow tool names." and WB-004: "Existing non-workflow Pi agent features are not deleted merely to migrate workflow agent()." -> in mode C and mode D the SubagentWorkflow and Agent tools are present with definitions deep-equal to mode A; with settings {workflowsEnabled:false} under mode C, 'SubagentWorkflow' is absent, the Agent tool is present, and the rest of the surface equals the pinned measured literal for that mode (recorded in the test, whichever it is).
4. docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md § "Current experimental policy surface": "Selecting Claude does not supply native grants." and § "Registration and resolution": "Discovery returns permitted metadata only; never implies invoke permission." and "Build a finite allowlist for each Pi tool, each Claude role/tool server and each workflow host; no 'everything registered = everything executable'." -> mode D (every listed grant) registers exactly the same tool-name set, commands, flags and tool definitions as mode C (zero grants): grants change what a tool answers, never what is registered; the pinned WORKBENCH_TOOLS literal is a finite allowlist and any registered name outside LEGACY_TOOLS ∪ WORKBENCH_TOOLS fails the census with a message naming the unexpected tool.
5. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Install profile": "Keep standard upstream features working when Workbench is disabled." -> in modes A and B none of the seven WORKBENCH_TOOLS names is registered, and the lifecycle handler keys registered (pi.on event names) are identical across A-D (pinned literal).
6. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." -> the closure receipt records four mutation runs against a scratch copy of the tree (M1 register workflow_observe twice; M2 remove the workflowAgentBackend === "claude" condition at index.ts:2480 so workbench tools register in mode A; M3 remove the workbenchToolsRegistered guard so a second session_start re-registers; M4 rename SubagentWorkflow under the claude branch only), each failing test/workbench-surface-census.test.ts, while the unmutated tree passes; the test header comment records the measuring command and base SHA for every pinned literal.
7. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Pure layout and keyboard reducers are unit-tested without a TTY." and docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Matrix by subsystem" (Security): "authorized narrow provider tool used | script crafted RPC cannot escalate rights" -> every mode boots hermetically (hermeticDir) with no live Claude, Forge or Furnace process and no network; the test never executes a registered tool, only inspects registrations; it runs under ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-surface-census.test.ts without a TTY.

Process: red-first (the census is written with the pinned literals asserted BEFORE measurement is pasted in, and the M1-M4 mutants are the standing red proof); ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on the new file; no any beyond what test/helpers/boot-extension.ts already exports; no inline imports; never weaken or delete existing tests (test/workflow-tool.test.ts, test/workbench-security-pi-tools.test.ts and the 14 wiring tests untouched); src/ and docs/TRACEABILITY.md untouched; base a650133 or later; forge run lint / typing / build / test green in the worktree (npm ci first in a fresh worktree).

• export interface ClaudeEvidenceRequest { readTranscript: (sessionId: string, cwd: string, limit: number) => Promise<readonly ClaudeTranscriptRow[]>; grants: () => readonly string[] (the LIVE grant set, re-read on every call); owningSessionNode: { nativeRef: NativeRef; evidenceRefs: readonly string[] } (the projection node the ref was listed on); sessionId: string; cwd: string; evidenceRef: string; windowLimit: number (1..100, the bounded window readClaudeTranscript accepts); maxBytes: number (1..65536); maxLines: number (1..200); timeoutMs: number (1..2147483647); signal: AbortSignal; capturedAt: () => string (injected clock; the module never calls Date.now) }.
• export interface ClaudeEvidenceContent { contract: typeof CLAUDE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT; kind: 'claude.transcript.message'; provider: 'claude-agent-sdk'; nativeRef: NativeRef ({provider:'claude-agent-sdk', type:'message', id: uuid, scope: sessionId}); role: 'user'|'assistant'|'system' (the row type); capturedAt; bytes: number (UTF-8 byte length of the selected row's text as returned by the reader); truncated: boolean (bytes > maxBytes or more than maxLines lines); preview: readonly string[] (the selected row's text split on newlines, each line through redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText then a local zero-width strip of U+200B-U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF, max 200 characters, at most maxLines lines, plus a final '… truncated (budget)' line whenever truncated); producerReceipt: { sessionId: string; windowLimit: number; returned: number (rows the reader returned); rowIndex: number (position of the selected row in that window) }; freshness: 'current' } — the docs/20 EvidenceContent shape minus store-level fields, so the claude EvidenceLoader of the wb-g1g.1 follow-up returns it after applying the owning node's freshness.
• export async function readClaudeMessageEvidence(request: ClaudeEvidenceRequest): Promise<ClaudeEvidenceContent> — preconditions before any read (each a CapabilityError, reader never called): grants() not an array, containing non-string entries or any wildcard entry (claude:*, *) -> 'authorization' ("unknown permission data"); missing the exact literal 'claude:transcript' (case-sensitive; 'claude:Transcript', 'transcript', 'claude:*' do not count) -> 'authorization' ("claude:transcript grant required"); owningSessionNode.nativeRef.provider !== 'claude-agent-sdk' || type !== 'session' || id !== sessionId -> 'authorization' ("evidence ref is not listed on a Claude session node of this scope"; a pre-init {provider:'pi-workflow', type:'agent-call'} node, index.ts:2683, is refused because it carries no native session identity); evidenceRef absent from owningSessionNode.evidenceRefs -> 'authorization' (a message of another session is unauthorized); evidenceRef not matching /^claude-message:([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,119})$/ -> 'validation'; windowLimit, maxBytes, maxLines or timeoutMs out of range, or sessionId/cwd empty -> 'validation'; signal already aborted -> 'transport' ("Claude evidence read cancelled before launch"). Exactly one readTranscript(sessionId, cwd, windowLimit) call, raced against request.signal and timeoutMs (abort -> 'transport'; timeout -> 'transport' naming the budget; the reader promise is abandoned, never awaited further). Row validation: every returned row must be an object with type in user|assistant|system, string uuid and string text, else 'unavailable' ("malformed transcript row shape"). Selection: the first row whose uuid === the requested uuid; none inside the returned window -> CapabilityError('transport', "message <uuid> is outside the bounded transcript window (<returned> of limit <windowLimit>)") — never a synthesized row, never a neighbouring row. A thrown reader error is rethrown as CapabilityError('unavailable', preview) where preview is the message through redactWorkbenchText capped at 200 characters, never verbatim. The content never retains the window: no field named rows, lines, message, messages, raw, data or payload, and no other row's text appears anywhere in JSON.stringify(content).

2. docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Types": "Grant gating is two-layered and exact-string: loaders are constructed only when the host grant set contains requiredGrant, and every load re-reads the live grant set so mid-view revocation refuses with unauthorized." and § "Owner rulings on the design conflicts" 6: "A new claude:transcript grant gates the loader, and the existing c transcript path adopts the same grant in the parent slice so the two paths cannot diverge." -> grants () => ['claude:transcript'] reads; each of [], ['transcript'], ['claude:*'], ['*'], ['CLAUDE:TRANSCRIPT'], ['claude:transcript '] and a non-array value rejects with 'authorization' before the reader is called (spy count 0); a grants function returning ['claude:transcript'] on the first call and [] on the second makes the first read succeed and the second refuse with 'authorization' (live re-read, mid-view revocation); the exported CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_GRANT equals the literal 'claude:transcript'.
3. docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Types": "every preview line passes the shared redaction and terminal sanitizers plus a loader-local zero-width strip; raw payloads are never retained" and docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Data retention and privacy": "Avoid raw prompts/tool bodies by default; store reference/short redacted preview ... UI fetches full text lazily subject to permission." -> a selected row whose text contains 'Authorization: Bearer abc123', '"api_key":"xyz"', '\x1b[31m', U+202E, U+200B and U+FEFF renders every preview line with the redaction marker and without escape, bidi or zero-width characters, each <= 200 characters; a 300-line row with maxLines 200 and a 70000-byte row with maxBytes 65536 each yield truncated true with the final '… truncated (budget)' line; for a window whose OTHER row carries 'OTHER-ROW-SECRET', that string and 'abc123' and 'xyz' appear zero times in JSON.stringify(content), and no key named rows, lines, message, messages, raw, data or payload exists on the content.
4. docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Authorization design": "Caller identity and scope bound at workbench entry point; impersonation from script payload prohibited." and § "Security acceptance tests": "cross-workspace ref returns authorization failure" and docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Proposed session tracker": "Mapping must distinguish workbench run ID, workflow agent ID, Claude SDK session ID, and optional native subagent IDs." -> an owning node {provider:'pi-workflow', type:'agent-call', id:'wf_1:0'} (pre-init, no native session), a node of another session id, a node whose provider is 'claude-agent-sdk' but type 'tool-use', and a ref not present in owningSessionNode.evidenceRefs each reject with 'authorization' and the reader is never called; the selected row's uuid, not the node id, becomes nativeRef.id.
5. docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Refusal and freshness rules": "A loaded entry never upgrades projection freshness and never changes node status text or tone. Transport success never implies verification." -> the content has no verified, status, statusTone, tone or outcome field and freshness is the literal 'current' (the owning node's freshness is applied by the loader/store per docs/20, not here); JSON.stringify(content) never contains '"verified"'.
6. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Key validations": "unrecognized SDK message version => diagnostic rather than silent success" -> rows with type 'tool', a numeric uuid, or a missing text each reject with 'unavailable' ("malformed transcript row shape"); a reader that throws Error('ENOENT /home/alice/.claude Bearer zzz') surfaces as CapabilityError('unavailable') whose message carries the redaction marker, lacks 'zzz' and is <= 200 characters; evidenceRef 'claude-message:' (empty uuid), 'claude-message:\x1b[31mx' and a 121-character uuid each reject with 'validation'.
7. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" (Details): "Large content loaded only on focus." and § "Rendering pipeline": "Pure layout and keyboard reducers are unit-tested without a TTY." and docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." -> the module performs exactly one readTranscript call per invocation (spy) and never calls any other injected function; a pre-aborted signal rejects with 'transport' before the reader is called (spy count 0); aborting the signal while the reader promise is pending rejects with 'transport' and the content promise never resolves; a reader slower than timeoutMs rejects with 'transport' naming the budget; the module source (read by the test) imports only ./claude-transcript.js, ./observation.js, ./capability-registry.js and ./redaction.js and contains none of 'node:', '@anthropic-ai', 'process.', 'Date.now', 'Math.random', 'import('; capturedAt comes from request.capturedAt; every test runs without the Claude SDK, a TTY or network.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/forge-evidence.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-forge-evidence.test.ts. Pure reader: readForgeOperationEvidence(ref, deps) validates a forge-operation:<operation_id> ref (validated id shape only; anything else is a validation refusal so the store can fall back to no-loader), checks the exact grant string forge:inspect (typed authorization denial otherwise; wildcards and prefixes never match), re-reads through an injected seam shaped like the registered forge read capability (readForgeGateStatus result, contract forge.gate.status/v1; fake seam in tests, no live forge in the default gate), and returns plain EvidenceContent-shaped data (kind, provider forge, capturedAt, bytes, truncated, bounded redacted preview). title: W15-E/VC-5: bounded Furnace Attempt log evidence reader for the docs/20 "furnace run" EvidenceLoader row (run/attempt/stream identity checks, attempt of another run is unauthorized, lossy/incomplete/paged reads load with truncated true, sanitized bounded preview lines, no raw payload retained, zero control verbs); EvidenceLoader wrapper and wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD 1fc74f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Producer mapping" binds the furnace row — ref "native Attempt id listed on the owning run node", resolution "the observer's bounded logs read with its run/attempt/stream identity checks; lossy, incomplete or paged reads are loaded with truncated true; an attempt belonging to another run is unauthorized", grant furnace:inspect — but nothing in src/ performs that read as evidence: FurnaceObserver.snapshot (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts:83-125) reads only the LAST attempt's stdout as a 512-byte FurnaceLogReference {attemptId, stream, complete, lossy, returned, nextCursor} for the reading, never for an operator-selected attempt or stderr, and discards the lines; the inspector details view prints evidenceRefs strings only ('Evidence / details · producer references, not fetched payload', src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:192). wb-g1g.1 (ready, dispatch-held) delivers the contract module src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts and the inspector slice; docs/20 § "Types" rules that loaders route provider-first and that "every preview line passes the shared redaction and terminal sanitizers plus a loader-local zero-width strip; raw payloads are never retained". The native surface already exists and is typed by FurnaceObserverClient.logs.read(id, {attempt, limit, stream:'stdout'|'stderr'}, {timeoutMs}) -> Response<LogsReadDto> {kind:'logs_read', requestId, data:{run_id, attempt_id, stream, complete, lossy, returned, next_cursor, lines}} (furnace-observer.ts:10-14 and :99-107).

Scope (atomic, I/O only through the injected client, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/furnace-evidence.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-furnace-evidence.test.ts; register and wire nothing; do not edit src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts, src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (does not exist yet; wb-g1g.1), src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts, src/index.ts or src/workbench/designer.ts.

• export const FURNACE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT = 'workbench.furnace-evidence/v1'.
• export interface FurnaceEvidenceRequest { client: Pick<FurnaceObserverClient,'logs'>; runId: string (/^frn-run-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,100}$/); workspaceRoot: string; owningRunNode: { nativeRef: NativeRef; evidenceRefs: readonly string[] } (the projection node the ref was listed on); attemptId: string (/^frn-atm-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,100}$/); stream: 'stdout' | 'stderr'; maxBytes: number (1..65536); maxLines: number (1..200); timeoutMs: number (1..2147483647); signal: AbortSignal; capturedAt: () => string (injected clock; the module never calls Date.now) }.
• export interface FurnaceEvidenceContent { contract: typeof FURNACE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT; kind: 'furnace.attempt.log'; provider: 'furnace'; nativeRef: NativeRef ({provider:'furnace', type:'attempt', id: attemptId, scope: workspaceRoot}); stream; capturedAt; bytes: number (the producer's returned count); truncated: boolean (lossy || !complete || next_cursor !== null || lines dropped by maxLines); preview: readonly string[] (each line through redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText then a local zero-width strip of U+200B-U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF, max 200 characters, at most maxLines lines, plus a final '… truncated (producer: lossy|incomplete|paged|budget)' line whenever truncated); producerReceipt: { requestId: string; complete: boolean; lossy: boolean; nextCursor: string | null }; freshness: 'current' } — the docs/20 EvidenceContent shape minus store-level fields, so the furnace EvidenceLoader of the wb-g1g.1 follow-up returns it after applying the owning node's freshness.
• export async function readFurnaceAttemptLogEvidence(request: FurnaceEvidenceRequest): Promise<FurnaceEvidenceContent> — preconditions before any client call (each a CapabilityError, no read performed): owningRunNode.nativeRef must equal {provider:'furnace', type:'run', id: runId, scope: workspaceRoot} else 'authorization' ("evidence ref is not listed on a furnace run node of this scope"); attemptId must appear in owningRunNode.evidenceRefs else 'authorization' (an attempt belonging to another run is unauthorized, docs/20); invalid ids, stream or budgets -> 'validation'; signal already aborted -> 'transport' ("Furnace evidence read cancelled before launch"). Exactly one client.logs.read(runId, {attempt: attemptId, limit: maxBytes, stream}, {timeoutMs}) call, raced against request.signal (abort -> 'transport'; the SDK promise is abandoned, never awaited further). Response validation mirrors furnace-observer.ts:101-104: response.kind !== 'logs_read' -> 'unavailable' ("response kind differs from requested native read"); data.run_id !== runId || data.attempt_id !== attemptId || data.stream !== stream -> 'authorization' (identity drift); non-array lines, non-integer returned, returned < 0 or returned > maxBytes, non-boolean complete/lossy, next_cursor not string|null -> 'unavailable' ("malformed native log shape"). Thrown SDK errors are rethrown as CapabilityError('unavailable', preview) where preview is the message through redactWorkbenchText capped at 200 characters, never verbatim.
• No control verb exists on the accepted client type (Pick<FurnaceObserverClient,'logs'>) and a runtime spy proof asserts runs.get/stop/pause/resume and work.retry are never called even when present on the injected object.

title: W21-B: observation recovery and bounded-query size benchmark receipt (ingest events/s, retained memory, disconnect -> stale -> reconnect-alone falsifier -> per-snapshot reconcile latency, evicted-cursor partial-gap detection, query/window/relations/events byte sizes) at 1k/100k default limits and 10k/100k bench-only limits; measurement-only, src untouched
description:
Gap (measured at rig 1fc74f0): docs/workbench/14 § "Performance benchmark" lists metrics no bench records: "observer ingest events/s and projection memory", "recover snapshot/cursor latency" and "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries". qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs (receipts cmd_9572ac580306, cmd_4ff4ffabcbe0) measures navigation only; wb-9x5.1 (W21, ready) measures grouped navigation/layout/terminal bytes; test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts:11 asserts one query's examined count (<4) and bytes (<2000) with no receipt and no recovery; test/workbench-observation.test.ts:43 proves "reconnect alone cannot restore current without snapshot" at toy scale only. The recovery API exists in src/workbench/observation.ts: disconnect():356, reconnect():369, refresh():318, markStale():344, events():540 (completeness "complete" | "partial-gap"), query():477, window():448, relations():397, stats():558, MAX_DEFAULT:93 {maxEvents 20000, maxNodes 2000, maxEdges 4000, maxPayloadBytes 4096, maxQuery 100}. furnace_observe (src/index.ts:2555-2563) polls once (maxPolls 1) and relies on projection.refresh/markStale for freshness, so recovery cost at scale is an unmeasured VC-4/VC-5 claim.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free; no production limit or behavior change):
• qa/workbench/observation-recovery-receipt.mjs (new, pure, no src/ or dist/ import): buildFixture({seed, nodes, events, providers}) -> plain data {snapshots: NativeSnapshot[], updates: ObservationEvent[], shape} (deterministic: no Date.now or Math.random in the measured path, timestamps derived from one fixed epoch, same rules as the header of test/helpers/perf-fixtures.ts; provider mix forge/furnace/claude-agent-sdk; one invocationId and one scope); measureRecovery(ProjectionClass, fixture, {limits?, provider, queryLimit}) -> measurement (exported so vitest passes the src class and the CLI passes the dist class); assessRecovery(measurement) -> {findings: {rule, detail}[], realised: boolean}; buildReceipt(input) -> frozen plain object {contract: "workbench.observation-recovery/v1", utc, revision, node, arch, platform, cpus, passes, findings, realised, pass}.
• measureRecovery, per pass: ingest every update (ingestMs, eventsPerSecond, applied/duplicate/out-of-order counts); retained = stats(); heapGrowthBytes labelled "transient-inclusive"; disconnect(provider) -> staleAfterDisconnect (nodes whose freshness !== "current", counted through bounded query pages) and disconnectMs; reconnect(provider) ALONE -> currentRegainedWithoutSnapshot (must be 0; otherwise finding "reconnect-restored-current"); refresh(snapshot) once per node of that provider -> per-call latency p50/p95/max over single refresh() calls and reconcileMs until that provider's stale count returns to 0 (otherwise finding "stale-after-full-refresh"); events({scope, limit: queryLimit, after: <a cursor older than the retained window>}) -> completeness must be "partial-gap" with gapDetectMs (otherwise finding "gap-not-detected"); events({after: <a retained cursor>}) -> "complete" with resumeMs; bounded query sizes: maxBytes of JSON.stringify for query({scope, invocationId, limit: queryLimit}), window({scope, invocationId, offset: 0, limit: queryLimit}), relations({scope, from: <key>, limit: queryLimit}) and events({scope, limit: queryLimit}) plus rowsReturned per method (rows > limit is finding "limit-exceeded"; any "\x1b" in a serialized result is finding "ansi-in-result").
• Two passes in ONE receipt: pass "default-limits" = new ProjectionClass() with no limits argument (caps never raised), 1,000 nodes / 100,000 events; pass "bench-only-limits" = new ProjectionClass({maxNodes: 12000, maxEdges: 24000, maxEvents: 20000, maxQuery: 100}), 10,000 nodes / 100,000 events, limits recorded in the receipt and never entering src/.
• qa/workbench/observation-recovery-bench.mjs (new CLI; imports ONLY ../../dist/workbench/observation.js, ./observation-recovery-receipt.mjs, node:os and node:fs): builds both fixtures, runs both passes, prints the receipt as one JSON line and writes it to $W21_RECOVERY_RECEIPT when set BEFORE exiting; exit 2 when a realised fixture shape is below 1,000/100,000 (pass A) or 10,000/100,000 (pass B) — the measurement would not be the claimed shape; exit 1 when findings is non-empty (a measured semantic violation, recorded honestly, never tuned away); exit 0 otherwise. No recovery-latency threshold exists in the specs, so latency is reported, never judged.
• test/workbench-observation-recovery-receipt.test.ts (new, offline): imports the receipt module; runs measureRecovery with the src ObservationProjection class (import from ../src/workbench/observation.js) on a 200-node / 2,000-event fixture and asserts every measurement field is a finite number, currentRegainedWithoutSnapshot === 0, staleAfterDisconnect equals the provider's node count, stale count 0 after the full refresh, partial-gap detected for an evicted cursor and complete for a retained one; asserts assessRecovery raises each finding for synthetic violating measurements; asserts fixture determinism (same seed -> identical JSON, different seed -> different); reads qa/workbench/observation-recovery-bench.mjs as text and asserts its import specifiers are exactly the allowed set and that the only "maxNodes" literal is inside the bench-only pass object (pass A constructs with no argument).
• forge.toml: one additive [build.commands.observation-recovery-bench] block (command "node qa/workbench/observation-recovery-bench.mjs", timeout 300), NOT added to the default [build] gate list (same placement as inspector-bench).

title: W14/VC-5-C: pure attention and bottleneck selector over ObservationProjection (waiting/stale/unknown/disconnected counts, top measured open intervals from source intervals, dependency-chain critical path only as partial-estimated else incomplete-trace with reasons; caller clock, bounded, sanitized); inspector and tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig 1fc74f0): docs/workbench/10 § "Four views" (Overview) requires "status and counts, compact nested tree, active operations, attention panel and top measured bottlenecks" with the critical path "shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete", and docs/workbench/09 § "Aggregates and profiling" requires measured-vs-estimated separation with "incomplete trace" whenever intervals or dependencies are missing. Today src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:156-157 prints two CONSTANT strings regardless of data ('Attention: stale/unknown is last-known state, not live progress.' and 'Critical path: incomplete trace (no complete dependency/interval proof).'), pinned by test/workbench-inspector.test.ts:112-116 and :195-198. Nothing in src/ computes attention items, bottlenecks or a dependency-chain estimate from observed data: grep -rn 'bottleneck\|criticalPath' src returns only designer.ts:183/236 (criticalPath "unestablished" for run comparisons; hot, untouched) and the inspector constants. wb-6ze.2 (ancestor aggregates in observation.ts) pins criticalPath 'unestablished' and lists "concurrency/critical-path profiling" out of scope; wb-6ze.1 owns the inspector file this run; wb-752.2 builds the workflow_observe reply. This bead supplies the pure selector both consumers wire later.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/attention.ts exporting
• ATTENTION_CONTRACT = "workbench.attention/v1".
• selectAttention(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "relations">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; now: string; limit?: number; bottlenecks?: number }): AttentionReport.
• AttentionReport = { contract: typeof ATTENTION_CONTRACT; basis: "observed"; now: string; examined: { nodes: number; truncated: boolean }; counts: { active; waiting; success; failure; unknown; stale; disconnected; withInterval; withoutInterval }; disconnectedProviders: string[]; bottlenecks: { key; nativeRef; title; tone; freshness; openMs: number; measured: true }[]; unmeasured: number; clockSkew: number; criticalPath: { label: "incomplete-trace"; reasons: ("no-dependency-edges" | "missing-intervals" | "open-intervals" | "hypothesis-edges" | "cycle" | "truncated")[] } | { label: "partial-estimated"; keys: string[]; measuredMs: number; coverage: { chainNodes: number; dependencyEdges: number }; caveat: string }; clockCaveat: string }.
• Rules. `now` is the CALLER's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now()). Nodes come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit: input.limit ?? 100}) call; examined.truncated propagates its truncated flag. openMs = now − interval.startedAt for nodes with statusTone 'active' or 'waiting' that have interval.startedAt and no endedAt; a producer startedAt later than now clamps openMs to 0 and increments clockSkew; nodes without an interval are counted in unmeasured and never ranked; ranking is openMs descending then key ascending (deterministic); bottlenecks.length <= input.bottlenecks ?? 5 and every entry carries measured: true. counts.stale = nodes with freshness !== 'current'; counts.disconnected = nodes with sourceConnectionState 'disconnected'; disconnectedProviders = sorted distinct nativeRef.provider of those nodes. Tones are counted separately (waiting is never folded into active or stale).
• criticalPath. Dependency edges come from projection.relations({scope, from: key, limit}) for examined keys only, kind 'dependency' only. 'partial-estimated' requires ALL of: at least one dependency edge among examined nodes; no 'hypothesis' edge among examined nodes; no cycle on dependency edges; query not truncated; every node on the chosen chain has a COMPLETE interval (startedAt and endedAt). measuredMs is the sum of complete interval durations along the longest-duration dependency chain (DAG longest path); keys lists that chain in dependency order; the caveat literal is "Observed dependency edges and complete source intervals only; missing edges do not imply independence." Anything else returns incomplete-trace carrying EVERY applicable reason. The label is never "exact" or "complete" and no number is emitted without the partial-estimated label.
• clockCaveat literal: "openMs uses the caller clock against producer startedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled."
• Every title passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts; do not edit) and is cut to 120 characters; control characters never survive; JSON.stringify(report).length < 16384 at limit 100 / bottlenecks 5.

Out of scope: rendering in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (wb-6ze.1 / wb-g1g.1 territory this run), the workflow_observe reply (wb-752.2) and src/index.ts, any edit to src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2 owns the aggregate API; this bead only CALLS query/relations), token/cost/retry metrics (no producer supplies them), designer.ts (hot).

Specs: docs/workbench/10 (Four views; Rendering pipeline; Failure and deception defenses; Timeline), 09 (Aggregates and profiling; Relationships are typed and provenanced; Freshness and ambiguity; Data retention and privacy), 14 (Truth labels and release gates), 02 WB-029.

Clean external install and minimal-permissions run succeeds." -> after npm run build, forge run install-minimal exits 0 in the worktree and its command id is recorded in the delivered ledger line; the outer receipt shows probe exit 0, censusBefore equal to censusAfter and probe.workflowValue 42.

C2. docs/workbench/12-security.md section "Credential boundaries": "Pi operator host/deployment owns credential sourcing; providers borrow secure SDK clients; no serialized clients/private tokens across worker channel." and section "Security acceptance tests": "secret env not displayed" -> the probe's process.env key set equals exactly ['HOME','LANG','PATH','TMPDIR'] even when the runner itself is started with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set to sentinel values; neither receipt contains any sentinel value (the vitest guard proves the lib with seeded values; the runner proves the spawned probe).

C3. docs/workbench/12-security.md section "Authorization design": "Separate discover, inspect, observe, invoke and control grants." and "Treat unknown permission data as deny." and docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-008: "Capability discoverability and capability invocation authorization are independent." -> probe.registryOutcomes records discoverEmpty 0, discoverGranted ['fixture.echo'], invokeWithDiscoverOnly 'authorization', invokeWithUndefinedGrants 'authorization', invokeGranted 'returned'.

C4. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-007: "Missing provider, unknown capability ID, schema mismatch and unavailable binding fail explicitly, not as null success." -> invoke('fixture.missing', ...) rejects with an Error whose name is 'CapabilityError' and whose category is 'unavailable'; the probe fails if the promise resolves to any value, null or undefined included.

C5. docs/workbench/12-security.md section "Worktree and concurrency safety": "Distinct agent workspaces must not accidentally share writable package state even if Forge caches immutable data." and docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Runtime and host requirements": "Workspace materialization pinned to correct basis and permissions." -> with the installed tree read-only, the probe's write attempt into node_modules/@tintinweb/pi-subagents fails with EACCES or EPERM (readOnlyEnforced true) unless the uid is privileged (then readOnlyEnforced false with reason 'privileged-uid', still recorded); treeCensus over the installed tree is identical before and after the probe in every case.

C6. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Development workspace": "Node/TypeScript versions and exact SDK versions should be pinned in lockfile and verified by a clean external consumer test." and docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-049: "Workbench release supports reproducible install and bounded per-provider optional dependencies." -> the outer receipt carries the tarball filename, shasum, integrity and fileCount from npm pack --json, and the probe asserts that the installed vendor/dependency-lock.json is among pinned.dependencyArtifacts (the same assertion installed-consumer.mjs makes), so the minimal run is proven against the packed artifact, not the developer tree.

C7. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Truth labels and release gates": "Every test evidence artifact includes revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output." and "Use Forge build/test/gates as primary interface" -> both receipts are single JSON lines; the outer one carries revision, node version, platform, arch, uid, utc and the exact npm and probe commands; forge.toml has [build.commands.install-minimal] with timeout 300 and the default gate array is byte-identical to before (guard test); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-install-minimal.test.ts is green with no network and no npm.

title: VC-7/W18-B: pure native executable identity observation (realpath + sha256 for absolute paths, PATH-resolved binaries labelled mutable-path, SDK default executable labelled unsupported, never executes) plus reattach comparison that never upgrades unknown to same; detached host wiring excluded
description:
Gap: docs/workbench/15 names "native immutable deployment refs" as VC-7 acceptance and docs/workbench/08 says native executable identity is an unestablished release obligation; W18 (wb-5w0) notes "Native binaries ... not claimed" and W22 (wb-cax) notes "Full release/install native binary identity ... remain open". At rig ad3cf6e the detached host hard-codes `nativeRuntimeIdentity: "unsupported"` (src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:82 and :96) and its runtimeClosure comment reads "Native executables launched by SDK defaults/PATH still have unsupported identity."; src/workbench/providers/forge.ts:80 launches ServerConnection.spawn("forge"), a bare PATH-resolved name; the Claude Agent SDK's Options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1984) "Uses the built-in executable if not specified." Nothing in src/ can observe, pin or compare the bytes of a native executable, so no host can honestly report which binary it launched or refuse reattachment when that binary changed.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/executable-identity.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT = 'workbench.executable-identity/v1'
- export type ExecutableIdentityReason = 'sdk-default-executable' | 'not-found' | 'not-a-file' | 'not-executable' | 'symlink-depth' | 'too-large' | 'unreadable' | 'path-resolved' | 'shadowed-candidates' | 'search-truncated' (frozen set; nothing else is ever emitted).
- export interface ExecutableObservation { contractVersion: typeof EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT; requested: string | undefined; resolution: 'absolute' | 'path-search' | 'unresolved'; resolvedPath?: string; realPath?: string; symlinkHops: number; digest?: string (sha256:<hex>); sizeBytes?: number; mode?: number; candidates: number; immutability: 'digest-observed' | 'mutable-path' | 'unsupported'; reasons: readonly ExecutableIdentityReason[]; observedAt: string }
- export function observeExecutableIdentity(input: { command: string | undefined; cwd: string; path: string | undefined; observedAt: string; maxBytes?: number; maxSearchEntries?: number; maxSymlinkHops?: number }): ExecutableObservation — synchronous; reads only through node:fs (lstat, readlink, stat, chunked reads for hashing — never readFileSync of a whole binary); never imports node:child_process; never reads process.env (PATH is an explicit input); never throws for a missing, unreadable, non-regular, non-executable or oversized target — those are 'unresolved'/'unsupported' with a reason.
  • command undefined or empty -> resolution 'unresolved', immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['sdk-default-executable'] (the honest answer for the Claude built-in executable and any SDK default).
  • command containing a path separator -> resolved against cwd; symlinks followed hop by hop (count hops; above maxSymlinkHops, default 16, -> 'unsupported' with 'symlink-depth'); must be a regular file with an execute bit; hashed with sha256 when sizeBytes <= maxBytes (default 512 MiB) -> resolution 'absolute', immutability 'digest-observed'; oversize -> digest omitted, immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['too-large'].
  • bare command -> PATH searched in order (split on path.delimiter; at most maxSearchEntries, default 64, further entries ignored and 'search-truncated' recorded; relative or empty entries resolved against cwd); the first regular executable file wins; candidates counts every searched entry holding a same-named executable; resolution 'path-search'; the digest IS observed but immutability is 'mutable-path' with reasons ['path-resolved'] plus 'shadowed-candidates' when candidates > 1. A digest never upgrades a PATH-resolved binary to 'digest-observed'.
  • Result and its reasons are frozen; resolvedPath and realPath pass through redactWorkbenchText (paths may embed tokens); absent fields mean not observed, never a default.
- export function compareExecutableIdentity(recorded: ExecutableObservation, current: ExecutableObservation): { verdict: 'same' | 'changed' | 'unknown'; differences: readonly string[] } — 'same' only when both digests are present and equal AND both immutability values are 'digest-observed'; 'changed' when both digests are present and differ; otherwise 'unknown' (a mutable-path or unsupported side can never yield 'same'); differences names each differing field (digest, realPath, sizeBytes, mode, immutability, resolution).

description:

D1. An effect that happened is never repeated and never reported as a verdict. In F1 the marker count for "effect-crash" is exactly 1 after the crash, after inspect() reports terminal "unknown" (observation "unknown", source "local-client-transport", reconcileHint matching /never.*retry|do not.*retry/i, no result field), after execute() rejected and after the same-id relaunch rejected /exists|conflict/; the snapshot never reports terminal "completed" or "failed" for that invocation. Required outcomes: reconciliation/uncertainty/conflict; no duplicate effects, no invented PASS, no implicit mass cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Optional local detached profile": "Inspection after host loss reports unknown with producer reconciliation guidance; it does not replay a saved terminal verdict or rerun JavaScript." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-026: "Interrupted effectful operation is reconciled through producer or marked uncertain; no automatic blind repeat."

D2. A lost result is not evidence the effect did not happen. The F1 receipt records effectObserved true (the marker exists) together with terminal "unknown", and the assessor records finding "effect-denied" if any journey field claims the effect did not occur. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "An observed timeout or disconnect is *not* evidence that side effect never happened." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md § "Nonfunctional invariants" NFR-02: "No host auto-retry of ambiguous irreversible writes."

D3. A deliberate second request is a new logical invocation, not a retry. "effect-crash-second" is accepted, writes exactly one marker of its own, and the receipt labels it explicitSecondRequest true with totalMarkers 2 across two ids; a relaunch under the ORIGINAL id stays refused. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Separate four identities": "Logical invocation: caller-created unique identity stable across retry of same request; distinct from identical intentional second request." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "A Pi UI reconnect is only an observer/client action; it must not restart external work."

D4. Cancellation has three phases and touches one host. In F2 cancel() returns { accepted: true, terminalConfirmed: false }; the next inspect() of "iso-a" shows cancellationRequested true before terminal "cancelled" appears; "iso-b" keeps observation "observed-running" or "observed-started", terminal undefined, cancellationRequested false and controlAudit [] throughout, and ends only by its own shutdown command. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Cancellation and ownership": "Multi-reader shared child MUST NOT be stopped merely because one reader closed Pi or stopped waiting." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Fault-injection locations": "Concurrent readers with one shared child; stopping one reader must not stop child without ownership."

D5. Shutdown reports unresolved effects honestly. In F3 shutdown of the running "unresolved" host returns unresolvedEffects true and of the never-executed "idle" host returns unresolvedEffects false; the later inspect() of "unresolved" is terminal "unknown" with a reconcileHint, never "completed". Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "Shutdown: stop accepting calls, notify owned local tasks, attempt graceful end, report unresolved effects, and release owned resources." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-041: "Optional detached workbench host permits Pi client disconnect/reconnect, without falsely claiming crash durability."

D6. SIGTERM is loss, not completion. In F4 inspect() after SIGTERM reaches terminal "unknown" within 5 s (latency recorded), execute() rejects, and the marker count is unchanged. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Lifetimes": "Detached service: independent process survives Pi client disconnect but does not guarantee service crash recovery." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "The local detached shell tier is a separate process-lifecycle proof, not remote authentication or native crash-durability evidence."

D7. Offline falsifiers in test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts: a journey with marker count 2 under one id -> finding "duplicate-effect"; terminal "completed" after crash -> finding "fabricated-terminal"; same-id relaunch accepted -> finding "reuse-after-loss"; sibling cancellationRequested true or terminal "cancelled" -> finding "mass-cancellation"; unresolvedEffects false for a running host -> finding "unresolved-effects-hidden"; a clean fixture -> pass true with every receipt field present; the generated provider text contains exactly one marker write before process.kill and none after. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Test classes" D: "Fault: ambiguous write timeout, process kill at every side-effect boundary, transport disconnect".

D8. Evidence-grade receipt and placement. The receipt carries contract "workbench.detached-faults/v1", utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD or the literal "working-tree"), node, arch, platform, per-journey timestamps and latencies, markerCounts, findings, realised and pass, and contains no absolute filesystem path (basenames and invocation ids only); forge.toml gains exactly one [build.commands.local-detached-faults] block (command "node qa/workbench/local-detached-faults.mjs", timeout 240) with the [build] gate list byte-for-byte unchanged (the test asserts both); npm run build && forge run local-detached-faults is executed in the worktree and its command id, exit code and receipt are recorded in the delivered ledger line; node qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs still exits 0. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Every test evidence artifact includes revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output." Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Vertical cuts" VC-7: "Remote host authentication, reattachment, native immutable deployment refs, crash/uncertain-operation conformance."

description:

Deliver: test/workbench-vendor-pins.test.ts (new vitest; node:crypto sha256 over vendor/*.tgz; parses the README markdown table rows `| <file> | <sha256> |`, package.json and package-lock.json; no network, no npm child process). Implement the checker as a pure function inside the test file (input: { readmeRows, tarballDigests, manifest, lock }, output: string[] of findings) so the same function runs against the real tree AND against in-memory negative fixtures: a README row with one hex digit changed -> finding naming the file and both digests; a `file:vendor/x.tgz` dependency absent from bundledDependencies -> finding; a lock entry with `inBundle: false` or a `resolved` that is not `file:vendor/<file>` -> finding; a tarball without a README row or without a package.json dependency -> orphan finding; a version in the filename that differs from the lock entry version -> finding.

Out of scope: changing vendor contents, versions, lockfile or package.json (if the real-tree run is red at rig HEAD, stop, record the mismatch in the ledger line and return blocked rather than editing pins); docs edits; src/ edits; forge.toml edits.

description:
